items.description: 给国产电视的一块干净桌面：参照 tvOS 设计的开源 Android TV 桌面，没有广告，开机自动接管。A tvOS-style launcher for Xiaomi, TCL and other China-market TVs.
items.readme:
# Aerial **给国产电视的一块干净桌面。** 参照 tvOS 设计的 Android TV 桌面：没有广告，没有推荐流，只有你的 App、你的壁纸和 Apple TV 航拍屏保。
为小米、TCL 等国产电视而做，开机自动接管，待机也不会被清理。 **中文** · [English](README.en.md) ![Aerial 首页](site/img/home.jpg) | 电视自带的桌面 | 换上 Aerial 之后 | |:---:|:---:| | | |
## 功能 ### 首页

- **时钟**：大号细体时钟压在壁纸上，壁纸底部和左侧自动压暗。往下滚动时，时钟收进状态栏。 - **应用网格**：每行 5 个，聚焦时浮起并显示名字。默认加一圈白色描边，离得远也看得清；在「控制中心 → Aerial 设置」可以改回 tvOS 的原样。 - **图标**：有电视横幅就用横幅；方形图标用自己的底色铺满磁贴；自适应图标拆成两层做视差。 - **全部 App**：小米「应用中心」「高清播放器」「米家」这类没有标准入口的系统 App 也会显示。 - **信号源磁贴**：把 HDMI、AV、电视天线固定到首页，按一下直接切换（控制中心 → 信号源 → 显示在主屏幕）。 - **返回键**：和 tvOS 一样，在网格里按返回回到第一行，在第一行按返回开始屏保。 ### 长按菜单 ![长按菜单](site/img/menu.jpg) 长按 OK 键：**移动**（其他磁贴自动让位）、**从主屏幕隐藏**、**应用信息**、**卸载**。 ### 控制中心 ![控制中心](site/img/control-center.jpg) 按遥控器的菜单键（≡）打开，或在第一行按上键。包括信号源（显示 CEC 设备）、网络、设置，音量和亮度滑块，以及壁纸与屏保、隐藏的 App、Aerial 设置。网络和设置会打开电视自己的面板。 ### 屏保

- **航拍**：114 段 Apple TV 航拍影片，从 Apple 的服务器直接播放，镜头移动时显示地名。左右键切换上一段 / 下一段。 - **照片**：每日精选和你的照片缓慢推移。 - **时钟**：每分钟换一个位置，防止烧屏。 在使用 Android 标准屏保的电视（比如 TCL）上，Aerial 就是系统屏保。小米用自家的屏保，Aerial 会在桌面空闲时抢先启动，挡在小米的广告屏保前面。 ### 壁纸与手机设置

- **壁纸**：必应每日精选（国内直连）、8 组内置渐变，或者你自己的照片。 - **用手机设置**：扫描壁纸面板上的二维码，在手机上传照片、选壁纸、换屏保。页面只在面板打开时开放，地址带随机令牌。 ## 安装 不需要 root，**不卸载、不停用任何系统应用**，一条命令就能还原。 ### 第一步：打开电视的 ADB 调试 电脑和电视连同一个网络。先在电视上找到 IP 地址（一般在「设置 → 网络」或「关于」里），再打开 ADB： | 电视 | 怎么打开 | |---|---| | **小米 / Redmi** | 设置 → 关于 → **产品型号**，连续按确认键，直到提示已进入开发者模式。再到 设置 → 账号与安全，打开 **ADB 调试** 和 **安装未知来源的应用** | | **TCL / 雷鸟** | 设置 → 关于 → **本机信息**，依次按遥控器的 **上、下、左、右**（间隔不超过 1 秒），底部会出现「更多」，在里面打开 **ADB** | | **原生 Android TV / Google TV**、海信等 | 设置 → 设备偏好设置 → 关于 → 连续按 **版本号** 7 次；再到 开发者选项 打开 **USB 调试**（也可能叫「网络调试」或「ADB 调试」） | 电脑第一次连接时，电视会问「允许 USB 调试吗？」，选 **允许** 并勾上「始终允许」。 ### 用 Agent 安装（推荐） 把下面这段交给 Claude Code、Codex、Cursor 这类能在你电脑上运行命令的 Agent，把 `<电视IP>` 换成你的电视 IP： ```text 请帮我把开源电视桌面 Aerial（https://github.com/pengchujin/aerial-tv）安装到我的电视上，并让它成为开机自动启动的桌面。 我的电视 IP 是：<电视IP> 请按这个顺序做： 1. 读一下仓库 README 的「安装」部分和 docs/devices/ 下的机型笔记。 2. 确认电脑上有 adb、curl、python3（没有 adb 也可以，安装脚本会自动下载 Google 的 platform-tools）。 3. 运行 adb connect <电视IP>:5555。连不上就提醒我按 README 在电视上打开 ADB 调试；显示 unauthorized 就提醒我在电视上点「允许」。 4. 运行一键安装： curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pengchujin/aerial-tv/main/tools/get.sh | KEEP_ADB=1 TV=<电视IP> bash 如果是 TCL，电视右上角会弹出「多屏互动：正在发起应用推送」，提醒我在电视上选「同意」。 5. 装完后用 adb shell dumpsys window | grep mCurrentFocus 确认前台是 app.orchard.tv；征得我同意后再 adb reboot 一次，确认开机直接进入 Aerial。 6. 不要卸载或停用任何系统应用，不要删除电视上不是这次安装创建的文件。失败时把命令输出原样给我看，再参考 docs/devices/ 排查。 ``` ### 一行命令（macOS / Linux） ```bash curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pengchujin/aerial-tv/main/tools/get.sh | KEEP_ADB=1 TV=192.168.1.20 bash ``` 脚本会下载最新版 APK 安装，授予只有 ADB 能给的权限（见下表），预编译让它更流畅，然后接管桌面和屏保、放行开机自启。 - `KEEP_ADB=1`：电视关掉 ADB 调试后（小米待机唤醒时会关），Aerial 立刻重新打开。不需要可以去掉。 - **固件拒绝安装桌面类 App**：在命令最后加 `-s guard`，改装不声明 HOME 的版本。 - **TCL**：TCL 拒绝一切 ADB 安装，脚本会改用电视自带的「多屏互动」推送，你在电视上选一次「同意」即可；没有多屏互动时退回用当贝市场。 还原成原来的桌面： ```bash curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pengchujin/aerial-tv/main/tools/get.sh | TV=192.168.1.20 bash -s restore ``` ### 手动安装 到 [Releases](https://github.com/pengchujin/aerial-tv/releases/latest) 下载 `aerial-standard.apk`（固件拒绝安装桌面类 App 时用 `aerial-guard.apk`），然后： ```bash adb connect 192.168.1.20:5555 adb install -r aerial-standard.apk adb shell pm grant app.orchard.tv android.permission.WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS adb shell cmd notification allow_listener app.orchard.tv/app.orchard.tv.guard.RevivalListener adb shell appops set app.orchard.tv SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW allow adb shell am start -n app.orchard.tv/.MainActivity ``` Aerial 启动后会自己打开桌面守护。屏保、亮度、TCL 自启等完整步骤见 [tools/install.sh](tools/install.sh)。 ## 它怎么接管桌面，又怎么不被杀掉 国产电视大多只认自家桌面，待机时还会清理第三方 App。Aerial 先温和、后强硬： 1. **正常申请**：申请 HOME 角色、设为默认桌面。原生 Android TV 和 Google TV 到这一步就够了。 2. **桌面守护**：固件坚持用自家桌面时（小米、TCL 都是），由一个无障碍服务接管：官方桌面一到前台，就把 Aerial 拉回来。它只看哪个窗口到了前台，不读屏幕内容。 3. **被杀后复活**：小米待机会强制停止所有第三方 App。Aerial 注册了一个通知监听（不读任何通知），系统会在约 0.5 秒内重新绑定它，Aerial 借此复活，并用 `WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS` 重新打开守护。 4. **开机自启**：开机时系统绑定通知监听，Aerial 随之启动。TCL 的「自启动管理」默认拦截第三方 App，安装脚本会用 `appops` 放行。 5. **ADB 常开**（可选）：小米唤醒后会关掉 ADB 调试，开了 `KEEP_ADB` 后 Aerial 会马上打开它，方便以后升级。 ### ADB 授予的权限 | 权限 | 用途 | |---|---| | `WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS` | 重新打开被系统关掉的守护；保持 Aerial 为系统屏保；`KEEP_ADB`；写入小米的背光值 | | 通知监听 | 被强制停止或开机后由系统拉起，不读取任何通知 | | 悬浮窗（`SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW`） | 开机后从后台打开 Aerial | | 修改系统设置 | 用标准接口调节亮度 | | 定位 | 只用来读取 Wi-Fi 名称 | | TCL `APP_AUTO_START` / `APP_ASSOC_START` | 允许开机自启（只有 TCL 有） | ## 已验证的电视 | 机型 | 系统 | 状态 | 笔记 | |---|---|---|---| | 小米 MiTV-MFTR0 | Android 14 / HyperOS TV | 日常使用中 | [笔记](docs/devices/xiaomi-mitv-mftr0.md) | | 小米 MiTV-MFFU0 | Android 14 / HyperOS TV | 安装、开机自启已验证 | [笔记](docs/devices/xiaomi-mitv-mffu0.md) | | Redmi X65 2026（MiTV-MFTR0） | Android 14 / HyperOS TV | 用户验证：安装、重启后自动进入（[#3](https://github.com/pengchujin/aerial-tv/issues/3)） | 同 MiTV-MFTR0 | | TCL MT5879 国行 | Android 11 | 日常使用中 | [笔记](docs/devices/tcl-mt5879-cn.md) | | 索尼 XRJ-77A80J 国行（BRAVIA VH2） | Android 10 | 用户验证：安装、开机自启、待机唤醒、屏保（[#16](https://github.com/pengchujin/aerial-tv/issues/16)） | — | | 索尼 BRAVIA VH1 国行 | Android 12 | 用户验证；亮度改为打开索尼的图像设置（[#2](https://github.com/pengchujin/aerial-tv/issues/2)） | — | 其他品牌（海信、创维等）应该也能用，但还没在真机上验证。欢迎[提交 Issue](https://github.com/pengchujin/aerial-tv/issues) 或 PR 补充你的机型。 ## 已知限制 - **需要联网**：航拍按 1080p H.264 实时播放，码率约 15–20 Mbps；每日精选也要联网。 - **HDMI 设备名**：真实名称（如「Apple TV」）需要系统权限才读得到，所以只显示「已连接」。 - **TCL 音量条**：调音量时会同时弹出 TCL 自己的音量条，这是让音量真正生效的必要条件。 - **小米屏保**：停在别的 App 里空闲时，仍然会出现小米自己的屏保。 - **网页安装**：浏览器连不上电视的网络 ADB，电视的 USB 口也不能被电脑当成设备连接，所以没法「打开网页就装」。 ## 开发 需要 JDK 17、Android SDK 36。 ```bash ./gradlew assembleStandardRelease assembleGuardRelease BUILD=1 KEEP_ADB=1 TV=<电视IP> tools/install.sh # 用本地编译的 APK 安装 ``` - [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md)：代码结构与数据流 - [docs/HANDOFF.md](docs/HANDOFF.md)：现状、调试技巧、必须遵守的规则 - [docs/devices/](docs/devices/)：各机型的实测笔记，包括 TCL 多屏互动的推送协议 - [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md)：给 AI 代理的开发说明 - [site/](site/)：官网（纯静态，中文 `/`、英文 `/en/`） 设计上的取舍：按 960×540dp 的画布等比缩放，不同密度的电视看起来一样；电视 GPU 很弱，每帧最多一次全屏绘制，空闲时不跑动画；焦点动画用弹簧，可以中途打断；字体用 Inter（OFL 许可）。 航拍目录 `app/src/main/assets/aerials.json` 由 Apple 公开的 `resources-16.tar` 生成，只有影片地址和地名，不含影片本身。 ## 许可 [MIT](LICENSE)。Inter 字体使用 [SIL Open Font License](FONT-LICENSE-OFL.txt)。 Aerial 是独立的开源项目，与 Apple、小米、TCL、索尼均无关联。航拍影片版权归 Apple 所有，由 Apple 的服务器直接播放；每日精选图片来自必应，版权归原作者所有。

items.description: A fast, ad-free home screen for Google TV, LG webOS and Samsung Tizen. One button to undo.
items.readme:
# Free My TV **A fast, ad-free home screen for Google TV, LG and Samsung TVs.** Trending picks from your own apps, the weather at a glance, and a look that follows the sunset.
Open source. Built with Claude Code. One button to undo. [**freemytv.io**](https://freemytv.io) · [Install](#install) · [LG TVs](#lg-tvs-webos) · [Samsung TVs](#samsung-tvs-tizen) · [Any TV](#any-tv) · [Make it yours](#make-it-yours)
## What you get - **No ads.** No sponsored rows, banners or autoplaying promos. Not one. - **Your apps, front and center.** The streaming apps you actually use, on a glass shelf. Pick them and their order right on the TV. - **Trending, not sponsored.** Three fresh picks every hour from what's trending this week and the latest releases, only from apps you already have. Movies and Shows get their own tabs. - **Weather and markets, one press away.** The hour-by-hour forecast, sunrise and sunset, and live crypto prices. - **Light by day, dark by night.** It follows your city's real sunset, the way your phone does. - **A screensaver to match.** Full-screen photos of the picks with a big glass clock. - **Fast.** 60 fps, every frame in 16.6 ms, on the TV's own chip. The home screen uses 96 MB of memory instead of 242 MB (−60%).
Measured on a 98″ TCL Google TV running Android 14. - **Set up on the TV.** Language, your city, temperature, theme, the weather and prices cards, which coins, and the apps on the shelf, in Free My TV's own settings. - **Safe.** No root. Nothing is uninstalled. One button brings back the factory home screen. ## Install About ten minutes. You need a Google TV or Android TV (Android 9 or newer) and a computer on the same Wi-Fi. ### The easy way: Claude Code 1. **On the TV**, turn on developer mode: Settings → System → About → press *Android TV OS build* 7 times. Then Settings → System → Developer options → turn on **USB debugging**. Write down the TV's IP address (Settings → Network & Internet). 2. **On your computer**, get the code: ```bash git clone https://github.com/simbasjungles/free-my-tv && cd free-my-tv ``` 3. **Open [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) in that folder** and say: > Install Free My TV on my TV at 192.168.1.50. I live in Lisbon. It installs the tools it needs, builds the app and puts it on your TV. Swap in your TV's IP and your city. 4. **On the TV**, open *Free My TV* → *Home Screen* → *Free My TV*, and accept the debugging prompt (tick *Always allow*). ### The manual way 1. **On the TV**, do step 1 above. 2. **Tools:** a JDK (17+), the Android SDK command-line tools (build-tools 34, platform android-34) and adb. On a Mac: ```bash brew install --cask temurin android-commandlinetools android-platform-tools sdkmanager "build-tools;34.0.0" "platforms;android-34" ``` On Linux, get OpenJDK 17, Android's command-line tools and adb from your package manager, then run the same `sdkmanager` line. On Windows, use WSL. 3. **Build:** ```bash ./build.sh ``` The first run creates `config.properties`. Set your city and your [TMDB key](#the-tmdb-key) there, then run it again. 4. **Install:** ```bash adb connect 192.168.1.50:5555 adb install -r FreeMyTV.apk ``` On TCL TVs, also let it run in the background (TCL blocks it by default, and the switch never starts): ```bash adb shell "appops set io.freemytv AUTO_START allow || appops set io.freemytv APP_AUTO_START allow" ``` 5. **On the TV**, open *Free My TV* → *Home Screen* → *Free My TV*. ## LG TVs (webOS) The same home screen as an LG app: the picks, the glass shelf with your apps, the drawer with inputs, weather and prices, day and night, Home Settings and the shelf editor. It installs through LG's own Developer Mode, with nothing rooted or changed on the TV. LG's home screen stays where it is, and Free My TV is one press of a number key away. You need an LG TV (webOS 3 or newer) and a computer on the same Wi-Fi, with Python 3. 1. **On the TV**, open the LG Content Store and install **Developer Mode**. Sign in with a free [LG developer account](https://webostv.developer.lge.com), turn on **Dev Mode Status** (the TV restarts), then turn on **Key Server**. Write down the IP address and the passphrase it shows. 2. **On your computer**, get the code and build. `config.properties` works as for Google TV (your city, your [TMDB key](#the-tmdb-key)): ```bash git clone https://github.com/simbasjungles/free-my-tv && cd free-my-tv python3 webos/build.py ``` 3. **Install.** The first time, it asks for the TV's passphrase; updates don't: ```bash python3 webos/install.py 192.168.1.50 ``` 4. **On the TV**, while Free My TV is open, hold a number key on the remote. From then on, that key opens it from anywhere. With Claude Code, say *"Install Free My TV on my LG TV at 192.168.1.50. I live in Lisbon."* It builds the app and hands you the install command, so you type the passphrase yourself. Developer Mode lasts about 40 days: open the Developer Mode app now and then and press **EXTEND**. To remove Free My TV, run `python3 webos/install.py 192.168.1.50 --uninstall`. ## Samsung TVs (Tizen) The same home screen as a Samsung app, with everything the LG one has: the picks, the shelf, the drawer with the inputs, the weather and the prices, day and night, and its own settings. It installs through Samsung's own Developer Mode, with nothing rooted or changed on the TV, and Samsung's home screen stays where it is. You need a Samsung TV from 2017 or newer (Tizen 3+) and a computer on the same Wi-Fi. 1. **On the TV**, open **Apps** and type `1 2 3 4 5` on the remote. Turn **Developer mode** on, type your computer's IP address in **Host PC IP**, and restart the TV. 2. **On your computer**, download [TizenBrew Installer](https://github.com/reisxd/TizenBrewInstaller/releases/latest), the community's installer for Samsung TVs, open it and connect to your TV. 3. **Install from GitHub:** type `simbasjungles/free-my-tv`. On 2023 and newer TVs it asks you to sign in to your Samsung account once, to sign the app for your TV. 4. **Straight to it:** in the TV's settings, under Start Screen Options, turn on **Autorun Last App**: the TV turns on into Free My TV. This build takes your city from the TV's time zone. For your exact city and the trending picks, build it with your own `config.properties` and [TMDB key](#the-tmdb-key): open the folder in Claude Code and say *"Install Free My TV on my Samsung TV at 192.168.1.50. I live in Lisbon."* It sets up Samsung's tools, and on 2023 and newer TVs you sign in to your Samsung account in the browser to make the certificate. ## Settings The first values come from `config.properties`, created by the first build (Google TV, LG and Samsung use the same file). Most of them can also be changed on the TV, in *Free My TV* → *Home Settings*, and the TV's choice wins: | Key | What it does | Default | |---|---|---| | `tmdb_key` | Your free TMDB key, for the picks | empty | | `tmdb_region` | Your country (two letters): which titles are on which app | `US` | | `latitude`, `longitude` | Your city, for the weather and the sunset | New York | | `city` | The name on the weather card | `Weather` | | `language` | `auto` (follows the TV), `en`, `es`, `pt`, `ru`, or `de` on Google TV | `auto` | | `show_crypto` | Show Binance crypto prices on home and screensaver | `true` | | `currency` | Crypto prices in `USD`, `EUR`, `BRL`… | `USD` | | `temperature` | `C`, `F` or `auto` | `auto` | | `disable_assistant` | Also turn off Google Assistant | `false` | Changed something? Run `./build.sh` and install again. Keep `freemytv.keystore`: updates are signed with it. ### The TMDB key Free, and it takes two minutes: create an account at [themoviedb.org](https://www.themoviedb.org/signup), then open [Settings → API](https://www.themoviedb.org/settings/api) and request a developer key. Paste the *API Read Access Token* (or the *API Key*) after `tmdb_key=`. It's your key: `config.properties` stays out of git. ## Going back On the TV: *Free My TV* → *Home Screen* → *Original*. The factory home screen, screensaver and every app come back exactly as they were. If the new home screen ever crashes three times in five minutes, it switches back by itself. To remove it for good, switch to *Original* first, then uninstall *Free My TV* (Settings → Apps). ## What it changes - It becomes the home screen and the screensaver. - It turns off, without uninstalling: - the stock home screen and screensaver; - Google TV's recovery home, Play Games and YouTube Music; - on TCL TVs, the TCL Channel, messages, store demo, hotel menu, manuals, mirroring and logging apps; - on Philco TVs, AI PONT (promo channels and app downloads) and the manual; - on Multilaser TVs, Anoki's screen-content recognition (ACR), the store demo and the manual; - Google Assistant, only with `disable_assistant=true`. - On TCL TVs, the remote's Netflix, YouTube and Prime buttons keep working through a small accessibility service that only reads those buttons. Pick what each one opens in *Free My TV* → *Remote Buttons*; *Original* turns the service off. - Picture, sound, inputs, remote pairing, Google services and the Play Store are on a protected list, checked before every change. - Apps that saved a Wi-Fi network are never turned off, since Android would erase the network. If the TV's first setup saved yours, the switch asks you to forget the network and connect again in Settings first (saved networks out of range don't show there; Claude Code can remove them). ## Any TV Free My TV runs on Google TV and Android TV: TCL, Sony, Hisense, Philips, Xiaomi and more, plus streamers like Chromecast with Google TV, the Google TV Streamer, onn 4K and NVIDIA Shield. And on [LG](#lg-tvs-webos) and [Samsung](#samsung-tvs-tizen) TVs, as an app. **Any other TV:** plug a Google TV streamer into HDMI and free that one. Same steps, same home screen. **A different brand or model:** ask Claude. Free My TV is made to be adapted by AI. Open the folder in Claude Code and say *"set it up for my Sony"*: it reads your TV, finds its home screen and its promo apps, updates the lists below and walks you through a test. [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md) tells it how. | What | Where | |---|---| | Apps to turn off | `DEBLOAT` in [`HomeMode.java`](app/src/io/freemytv/HomeMode.java) | | Apps never to touch | `PROTECTED` in the same file | | Apps on the shelf | `SHELF` in [`HomeApps.java`](app/src/io/freemytv/HomeApps.java) | | Your brand's live TV app | `LIVE_TV_APPS` in the same file | ## Make it yours It's your code, and Claude Code finds its way around it. Try: - *"Add Crunchyroll to the shelf."* - *"Show the prices in euros."* - *"Add Spanish."* - *"Switch to the night look an hour after sunset."* ## How it works - **A plain Android app, no Gradle, no libraries.** [`build.sh`](build.sh) runs aapt2 → javac → d8 → zipalign → apksigner and makes a 2 MB APK. - **It uses the TV's own ADB, from inside the TV.** The app connects to `127.0.0.1:5555` with its own key (that's the *Allow USB debugging?* prompt) and runs the same commands you would: `cmd package set-home-activity`, `settings put secure screensaver_components`, `pm disable-user`. Nothing listens to the network. - **Drawn by hand on one Canvas**, with Android 13 shaders for the frosted glass and the sky (plain fills on Android 9 to 12, with lighter shadows and no GPU layers on 9 to 11 for their older GPUs). - **A safety net.** A watchdog in a separate process brings back the stock home screen after three crashes in five minutes, and a boot check keeps your choice after TV updates. - **On LG and Samsung, the same design in plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript** ([`web/`](web)), written for the Chromium of older TVs, with no frameworks. [`tizen/build.py`](tizen/build.py) packs the same app into a Samsung `.wgt`, which uses Tizen's web APIs for the apps and the inputs. To preview it on a computer: `python3 webos/build.py --preview`, then open `out/webos/index.html` (a stand-in lists sample apps). - **Data** from TMDB (trending titles, new releases and which app streams what in your country), Open-Meteo (forecast, sunrise and sunset), and optionally Binance (24-hour prices when `show_crypto=true`). | File | What it is | |---|---| | [`HomeView.java`](app/src/io/freemytv/HomeView.java) | The home screen | | [`HomeMode.java`](app/src/io/freemytv/HomeMode.java) | Switching between Free My TV and Original | | [`Adb.java`](app/src/io/freemytv/Adb.java) | The TV's own ADB, from inside the TV | | [`Recs.java`](app/src/io/freemytv/Recs.java) | The picks (TMDB) | | [`HomeData.java`](app/src/io/freemytv/HomeData.java) | Weather and prices | | [`HomeApps.java`](app/src/io/freemytv/HomeApps.java) | The shelf, inputs and All Apps | | [`DreamView.java`](app/src/io/freemytv/DreamView.java) | The screensaver | | [`SettingsActivity.java`](app/src/io/freemytv/SettingsActivity.java) | The settings screen (the app's icon) | | [`Prefs.java`](app/src/io/freemytv/Prefs.java) | Settings changed on the TV | | [`RemoteKeys.java`](app/src/io/freemytv/RemoteKeys.java) | The TCL remote's app buttons | | [`Watchdog.java`](app/src/io/freemytv/Watchdog.java) | The safety net | | [`web/home.js`](web/home.js) | The home screen on LG TVs | | [`web/tv.js`](web/tv.js) | The TV's apps and inputs, on LG and Samsung | | [`webos/build.py`](webos/build.py), [`webos/install.py`](webos/install.py) | The LG app package and its install | | [`tizen/build.py`](tizen/build.py) | The Samsung app package | The website ([freemytv.io](https://freemytv.io)) is in [`docs/`](docs): plain HTML, CSS and JS on GitHub Pages. ## Privacy No accounts, no analytics, no tracking. items.readme:
# 中国初中数学（七—九年级）知识图谱 · 第一版草稿

用「知识点节点 + 先修边」的有向无环图（DAG）描述人教版初中数学（七上至九下）的知识结构，数据格式参考 [Marble os-taxonomy](https://github.com/withmarbleapp/os-taxonomy)（`topics` + `dependencies`）。

> **状态声明：这是 AI 生成的初稿，未经任何教师审核。**
> 知识点的拆分粒度、掌握标准、诊断题答案，尤其是**先修关系（哪些是 hard、哪些是 soft，甚至某条边该不该存在）都需要一线初中数学教师审核**后才能用于教学、诊断或学习路径推荐。诊断题答案虽经抽查心算，但没有逐题由人工复核。

## 数据来源与对齐依据

- **课程标准**：教育部《义务教育数学课程标准（2022年版）》第四学段（7—9 年级）的内容范围与学段要求（数与代数、图形与几何、统计与概率、综合与实践四个领域）。第三轮起，课标第四学段【内容要求】已拆成机器可读条目（`data/cn-curriculum-standards.json`，157 条），每个正式知识点通过 `standards` 字段挂接 1–3 条（共 383 条映射）；来源、规则、覆盖率与局限见 [docs/standards-mapping.md](docs/standards-mapping.md)。
- **教材顺序**：人民教育出版社（人教版）义务教育教科书数学，**采用 2024 年审定的新版**。章节目录取自第三方电子课本目录站 dzskb.com（非人教社官方页面），核对情况如下：

  | 册次 | 采用的目录 | 核实情况 |
  |---|---|---|
  | 七上 | 第一章 有理数 … 第六章 几何图形初步 | 已核对目录页 |
  | 七下 | 第七章 相交线与平行线 … 第十二章 数据的收集、整理与描述 | 已核对目录页 |
  | 八上 | 第十三章 三角形 … 第十八章 分式（2024 审定版） | 已核对目录页 |
  | 八下 | 第十九章 二次根式 … 第二十四章 数据的分析（2024 审定版） | 已核对目录页 |
  | 九上 | 第二十五章 一元二次方程 … 第三十章 直线与圆的位置关系（2024 审定版） | 已核对目录页 |
  | 九下 | 第三十一章 相似；第三十二章 锐角三角函数（章末综合与实践：停车设计问题）；第三十三章 投影与视图（章末综合与实践：建筑中的数学）；第三十四章 随机事件的概率（34.1.1 随机事件，34.1.2 概率，34.2 用列举法求概率，34.3 用频率估计概率） | **非官方、待核**，详见下方「九下目录的来源与核实情况」 |

  新版教材相对旧版有较大调整（如多边形移入八下“四边形”、反比例函数移入九上、新增“数据的四分位数”“综合与实践”主题、概率由九上移到九下并改名“随机事件的概率”等），本图谱按新版目录处理。

### 九下目录的来源与核实情况（查证日期：2026-10-17；**非官方、待核**）

**结论**：没有找到人教社（pep.com.cn）官方发布的 2024 版九下目录页（官方“新教材介绍”页只介绍编写思路，未列各册章目；pep.com.cn 的“数学 九年级下册”页是旧版封面，页面不显示目录）。九下的 2024 版教材预计 2027 年春季学期才开始使用。下列目录是综合第三方来源后的**最可靠推定**，并非官方原文，章名、章号请以教材实物或人教社官方目录为准。

| 章 | 采用的章名 | 依据 |
|---|---|---|
| 第三十一章 | 相似 | 来源 A（搜索摘要）；与来源 D 的九上末章“第三十章”衔接 |
| 第三十二章 | 锐角三角函数；章末“综合与实践：停车设计问题” | 来源 A（搜索摘要） |
| 第三十三章 | 投影与视图；章末“综合与实践：建筑中的数学” | 来源 A（搜索摘要） |
| 第三十四章 | 随机事件的概率：34.1.1 随机事件、34.1.2 概率、34.2 用列举法求概率、34.3 用频率估计概率 | 来源 B、C |

来源：
- A：知乎专栏《2024年秋季学期修订人教版初中数学7-9年级教材目录》https://zhuanlan.zhihu.com/p/706262283 。正文需登录无法读取，**只看到搜索结果摘要**：“九年级下册：第三十一章相似 第三十二章锐角三角函数 综合与实践：停车设计问题 第三十三章投影与视图 综合与实践：建筑中的数学 第三十四章随机……”（摘要在此截断）。
- B：LibreMath 教辅页 https://libremath.cn/textbook/renjiao-jiuxia-sui-ji-shi-jian-de-gai-lv/ ，标称“人教版（2024 审定）九年级下册第三十四章《随机事件的概率》”，列出 34.1.1—34.3 各小节，并说明 2027 春起使用、章名由“概率初步”改为“随机事件的概率”。第三方教辅，非官方。
- C：21cnjy 新教材九下页的搜索摘要（https://mip.21cnjy.com/mulu/7/326226-2.html ，页面本身抓取超时）：“第三十四章随机事件的概率 34.1 随机事件与概率 34.2 用列举法求概率 ……”，与 B 一致。
- D：电子课本网 dzskb.com 的九上 2024 页 https://www.dzskb.com/rjbsx9sc-2024.html ，九上为第二十五至第三十章（反比例函数已在九上第二十七章），所以九下从第三十一章起，与 A 衔接。

**未采用的来源**：dzskb.com 标为“2024 审定版（现行）”的九下页 https://www.dzskb.com/rjbsx9sce-2024.html 列出的是“第二十六章 反比例函数 / 二十七 相似 / 二十八 锐角三角函数 / 二十九 投影与视图”，与同站旧版页内容完全相同，且与它自己的九上 2024 页矛盾（反比例函数不可能同时在九上第二十七章和九下第二十六章），判断为误标的旧版目录，不采用。

**仍待核的部分**：(1) 第三十一至三十三章的**小节号**没有查到，`chapter` 字段只写到章，不写小节号；第三十四章小节号来自 B、C。(2) “综合与实践”两项只来自来源 A 的摘要，活动的具体内容未核实，`cnm_290`、`cnm_291` 的描述与先修边是按主题名推定的。(3) 章内知识点是沿用第一版的拆分，没有逐节对照新教材。(4) 第三十四章章名“随机事件的概率”来自 B、C 两个第三方来源，来源 A 的摘要被截断。
- **小学先修**：18 个外部节点（`cnm_ext_*`）按小学数学课程内容概括，只作为图的根，不展开其内部结构。
- **格式参考**：已阅读 Marble 的 `data/topics.json` / `data/dependencies.json`（节点含 `type`、`domain`、`evidence`、`assessmentPrompt`；边为 `topicId` 依赖 `prerequisiteId`）。其中文分支 [os-taxonomy-beijing](https://github.com/luw2007/os-taxonomy-beijing) 只读了 README，**没有解析它的数据文件**。本项目在字段含义上对应关系为：`mastery_criteria` ≈ `evidence`，`diagnostic_question` ≈ `assessmentPrompt`；但文件顶层是裸数组（没有 `version`/`topicCount` 包装），id 为 `cnm_NNN`，也没有 `centrality`、`ageRange`、`standards`。

## 文件

```
data/topics.json         知识点节点（JSON 数组）
data/dependencies.json   先修边（JSON 数组）
data/cn-curriculum-standards.json  课标第四学段内容要求条目（157 条）
docs/standards-mapping.md          课标对齐说明：来源、映射规则、覆盖率、未映射清单、局限
data/questions.json      题库：每个正式知识点 4–5 题（共 1407 题）
data/verification_report.json  题库答案核验报告（自动核验 + 独立第二遍复核）
data/second_pass_log.json      第二遍复核的裁决与修正记录；data/_second_pass/ 是解题者的原始答案和推导
docs/questions.md                题库格式、核验方法、统计、局限
scripts/validate.py      校验脚本（仅标准库；含题库检查）
scripts/verify_questions.py  题库答案自动核验（受限表达式求值）
scripts/second_pass.py       独立第二遍复核的辅助脚本（出盲解题、比对答案）
CHANGELOG.md             按日期记录的变更日志（含 id 变动说明）
index.html               单文件浏览页面（无外部依赖）
diagnose/                诊断小工具（纯静态：index.html、engine.js、app.js、style.css、README.md）
tests/test_engine.js     诊断引擎测试（Node，无依赖）
scripts/screenshot.js    无头 Chrome 冒烟测试与截图脚本
screenshots/             诊断小工具截图（01-start / 02-question / 03-result / 04-graph / 05-explanation）
```

### topics.json 字段

正式知识点（`external: false`）：

| 字段 | 说明 |
|---|---|
| `id` | 稳定 id，`cnm_001` … |
| `name` | 中文名称 |
| `domain` | 数与代数 / 图形与几何 / 统计与概率 / 综合与实践 |
| `grade` | 7 / 8 / 9（整数） |
| `semester` | "上" 或 "下" |
| `chapter` | 人教版章节，如 `七上 第一章 有理数 1.2.1` |
| `type` | conceptual / procedural / reasoning / application / modeling |
| `description` | 通俗说明（1—2 句） |
| `mastery_criteria` | 2—3 条掌握标准（字符串数组） |
| `diagnostic_question` | `{"question": "...", "answer": "..."}` |
| `external` | `false` |
| `standards` | 课标映射数组，元素 `{"id", "confidence", "note"?}`，见下节；可为空数组 |
| `root_reason` | 仅当非外部节点没有任何先修边时必填（本版没有这样的节点，见下） |

外部（小学先修）节点：只有 `id`、`name`、`domain`、`grade`（固定为 `"小学"`）、`description`、`external: true`，另有 `standards: []`（本版没有做第三学段课标条目）。

说明：
- 数学里函数归“数与代数”，点的坐标、图形变换归“图形与几何”（与课标领域划分一致）。
- “综合与实践”节点（如 `设计学校田径运动会比赛场地`）是教材中的主题活动，按 `modeling` 处理，诊断题只是对活动中某一数学要点的检查。
- `一元二次方程根与系数的关系（拓展）`：课标要求“了解”（例67），第三轮已据此更正描述；名称里的“（拓展）”保留，其是否作为必学请教师判断。

### dependencies.json 字段

```json
{"topicId": "A", "prerequisiteId": "B", "strength": "hard", "reason": "一句中文理由"}
```

含义：**A 依赖 B**（学 A 之前需要 B）。

- `hard`：不会 B 基本无法学 A；`soft`：会 B 对学 A 明显有帮助（类比、简化、背景），但不是硬门槛。**这个区分是 AI 的主观判断，未经审核。**
- 只保留直接先修关系，并做了传递约简：`hard` 边仅在存在另一条全 `hard` 路径时才被删除，`soft` 边在存在任何其他路径时即被删除（生成时共剔除 90 条冗余边）。因此若看到某条边“缺失”，通常是已经能由更近的先修推出。
- 由于每个正式知识点最终都能追溯到至少一个小学外部节点，**本版没有需要 `root_reason` 的根节点**；图的根全部是 `cnm_ext_*`。

## 当前统计（`python3 scripts/validate.py` 实际输出）

- 知识点总数 **333**：正式 **315**，小学外部 **18**
- 按领域（正式）：数与代数 142，图形与几何 117，统计与概率 **43**，综合与实践 13
- 按册次（正式）：七上 61，七下 58，八上 57，八下 57，九上 49，九下 33
- 按类型（正式）：conceptual 102，procedural 101，reasoning 58，modeling 31，application 23
- 先修边 **616** 条：hard 497，soft 119；其中 53 条指向小学外部节点；正式知识点平均 1.92 条先修
- 未被任何知识点依赖的末端节点 63 个

## 第二轮迭代（2026-10-17）改了什么

详见 `CHANGELOG.md`。要点：

1. **九下章目核实**：去掉所有“（暂拟）”，九下 `chapter` 改为第三十一至三十四章的实际章名（来源与“非官方、待核”说明见上）。原九下 22 个知识点的 id 全部不变；章名由“概率初步”改为“随机事件的概率”，并给概率各点补上 34.1.1/34.1.2/34.2/34.3 小节号。新增两个章末“综合与实践”（`cnm_290` 停车设计问题、`cnm_291` 建筑中的数学）。
2. **统计与概率加厚**：领域“统计与概率”正式知识点由 **20 增至 43**（新增 23）。分布：七下 17、八下 12、九下 14。七上、八上、九上在新版教材里没有统计与概率章，所以没有硬凑。另有 3 个相关的“综合与实践”（`cnm_109`、`cnm_218` 原有，`cnm_315` 新增），不计入上面的 43。
3. **边**：新增 50 条（含统计新点的先修边及 `cnm_288`←`cnm_297` 等连接原有统计点的边），删除 1 条冗余边（`cnm_288`←`cnm_106`，已可经新增的 `cnm_297` 到达）；原有 287 条理由少于 8 个汉字的边，再加 79 条仍只有短语的边，共 366 条理由改写成完整一句话（最短的也有 9 个汉字以上）。
4. 没有改动 `scripts/validate.py`。

## 课标对齐（第三轮）

- **课标条目**：`data/cn-curriculum-standards.json`，教育部《义务教育数学课程标准（2022年版）》第四学段【内容要求】共 **157** 条：数与代数 49、图形与几何 92、统计与概率 13、综合与实践 3。id 形如 `cms-2022:4.NA.01`（NA 数与代数、GG 图形与几何、SP 统计与概率、IP 综合与实践），条文是课标原文，来自教育部官网 PDF。
- **知识点映射**：每个正式知识点的 `standards` 数组为 `{"id": "cms-2022:4.NA.17", "confidence": "exact"|"inferred", "note": "..."}`；exact 表示条款正文直接点名，inferred 表示前提、特例、延伸或教材细化，必须写 note。
- **覆盖率**：315 个正式知识点中 **313 个（99.4%）** 有映射；2 个未映射（`cnm_130` 辅助线与模型、`cnm_192` 折叠与动点问题）。另有 15 条课标条款没有对应知识点（多为作图、欣赏类和选学内容），列在文档里。
- **全部说明**（来源与 URL、检索日期、映射规则、覆盖率、未映射清单、已知局限）见 [docs/standards-mapping.md](docs/standards-mapping.md)。映射由 AI 生成，未经课程专家审核。
- 小学外部节点的 `standards` 为空数组，没有建第三学段（`cms-2022:3.*`）条目。
- `STRICT_STANDARDS=1 python3 scripts/validate.py` 会把“正式知识点 standards 为空”当作错误；默认只打印警告。

## 统计与概率知识点的教材落册（第二轮后）

- 七下 第十二章（17 个）：调查方式与样本（`cnm_102`—`cnm_104`、`cnm_298`、`cnm_299`、`cnm_300`），数据整理与统计图（`cnm_105`、`cnm_292`—`cnm_297`），直方图与趋势图（`cnm_106`—`cnm_108`、`cnm_301`）。
- 八下 第二十四章（12 个）：平均数、加权平均数、中位数、众数、方差、四分位数、分组数据及新增的样本估计总体、极端值、方差比较、箱线图。
- 九下 第三十四章（14 个）：随机事件、概率意义、列举法、列表法与树状图、频率估计概率、游戏公平性，以及新增的可能性排序、概率性质、等可能判断、放回与不放回、三步树状图、实际估计、统计图表综合、误解辨析。
- 小节号（如 12.1.2、24.2）是按第一版已有标注推定的，没有逐节核对新教材。新增的 `cnm_305`（箱线图）是否为教材必学内容、`cnm_315`（用随机试验检验游戏的公平性）是补充课题，均已在描述里标明，请教师取舍。

## 诊断小工具（第四轮；第五轮改为每个知识点最多 2 题）

`diagnose/` 是一个基于上述数据的静态、可离线的诊断页面：选一个目标知识点（或整个章节），按先修关系自适应出题（第一题答对则掌握并跳过全部祖先；答错则再出一道同级或更容易的题——第二题也错才算薄弱并回溯到先修，hard 先于 soft；第二题答对标为「不稳」，不回溯），给出薄弱的根因、不稳的知识点、按拓扑序排列的学习路径、相关课标条目原文和一张纯 SVG 路径图；每题作答后显示解析和参考答案；进度保存在 localStorage，可导出 JSON 或打印。核心算法与判题在 `diagnose/engine.js`（纯函数，浏览器与 Node 通用），由 `node tests/test_engine.js` 测试。

```bash
python3 -m http.server 8000
# 访问 http://localhost:8000/diagnose/            （演示：?target=cnm_221&demo=1）
node tests/test_engine.js                          # 引擎测试
node scripts/screenshot.js                         # 冒烟测试 + 截图（需要本机 Chrome）
```

算法说明、判题规则、URL 参数与局限见 [diagnose/README.md](diagnose/README.md)；浏览页 `index.html` 右上角也有入口。每个知识点最多问 2 题，诊断结果只是线索。

## 题库（第五轮）

`data/questions.json`：给 315 个正式知识点各建 4–5 道题，**共 1407 题**；`topics.json` 里原有的 `diagnostic_question` 迁移为每个知识点的第 1 题（id 后缀 `_q1`），原字段保留不动。

| 统计 | 数量 |
|---|---|
| 按 type | numeric 903，choice 475，short 23，self 6（numeric + choice 占 97.9%） |
| 按 difficulty | basic 591，standard 537，advanced 279（每个知识点都含 basic 和 standard） |
| 每知识点题数 | 最少 4，最多 5，平均 4.47（4 题 × 168，5 题 × 147） |
| 自动核验（`verify` 表达式） | 875 题通过，mismatch 0，unverifiable 532（主要是文字选项的选择题） |
| 独立第二遍复核 | 1401 题盲解比对，原始不一致 3 处（全是解题者算错），发现并修正答案错误 0 处，另改 4 处含糊题干 + 1 处错误解析；`second_pass_mismatch` = 0 |

```bash
python3 scripts/verify_questions.py   # 自动核验，写 data/verification_report.json；mismatch 为 0 才打印 VERIFICATION PASSED
python3 scripts/validate.py           # 含题库格式检查与题量统计
```

题目与答案全部由 AI 生成、未经教师审核，复核者与出题者是同一模型家族；格式、核验方法、统计与局限见 [docs/questions.md](docs/questions.md)。

## 已知局限

- **审核缺位**：见开头状态声明；先修关系、hard/soft 强度、诊断题难度与区分度都没有经过教师或学生数据检验。
- **覆盖不均**：统计与概率现为 43 个，但全部集中在七下、八下、九下三册（新教材只在这三册安排统计与概率，不含七上、八上、九上）；九下目录为第三方来源推定，非官方、待核（见上）；教材中的“阅读与思考”“数学活动”“小结”“信息技术应用”等栏目没有单独成点，仅少数“综合与实践”“探究与发现”并入。
- **粒度不统一**：个别知识点（如各类应用题）按题型归并，个别（如三角形全等的各判定）拆得较细，需按实际教学再调。
- **题库很小**：每个知识点 4–5 题、诊断时最多问 2 题，题与答案由 AI 生成、未经教师审核，难度与干扰项没有学生数据校准，不能代替完整测评。
- **按教材顺序推断**：部分先修边（如命题、定理类内容）反映的是教材编排而非严格逻辑依赖，已尽量标为 `soft`。

## 运行校验

```bash
python3 scripts/validate.py
```

检查：JSON 合法；id 唯一；必填字段齐全；`domain`/`type`/`strength` 取值合法；每条边的两端都存在；无自环、无重复边；无环（有环时打印环路）；每个非外部知识点要么有先修边要么有 `root_reason`；没有完全孤立的节点。并打印按领域、按册次的数量以及边数、hard/soft 数。第三轮新增：`standards` 引用的课标 id 必须存在于 `data/cn-curriculum-standards.json`，`confidence` 只能是 `exact`/`inferred`，课标文件自身的 id 格式与编号连续性；并打印课标条目数、映射覆盖率；正式知识点 `standards` 为空时只打印警告（至多 30 个），设置 `STRICT_STANDARDS=1` 才视为错误。全部通过时输出 `VALIDATION PASSED` 且退出码为 0，否则输出错误并以非 0 退出。

## 打开浏览页面

页面通过 `fetch` 读取 `data/*.json`，浏览器不允许直接用 `file://` 打开，请在本目录启动一个静态服务器：

```bash
python3 -m http.server 8000
# 然后访问 http://localhost:8000/
```

功能：左侧可按学科、年级/册次、类型筛选并搜索（名称、描述、章节）；可勾选是否显示小学先修节点。点击知识点后显示描述、掌握标准、诊断题（答案默认折叠）、**先修链**（向上递归，树状或分层列表两种视图，边上标注硬/软先修及理由），以及**它是哪些后续知识点的先修**。地址栏 `#cnm_219` 形式的 hash 可直接定位到某个知识点。

## 后续建议

1. 请初中数学教师先审先修边（尤其是 hard 边），并用教材实物或人教社官方目录核对九下的章名、章号和小节号。
2. 请课程专家审核 `standards` 映射（尤其 inferred），并考虑为 15 条无对应知识点的课标条款补点；再补充每个知识点的常见错误、典型例题。
3. 用真实学生答题数据校准诊断题与先修强度。

items.readme:
# GPU unlock 1.0.0

Unlock FP/BF16 instruction issue rate on Nvidia 3000's cards to their professional equivalents

This Linux kernel module combines the CMP unlocker's V67/PLM technique with the pre-driver timing of the UEFI approach. It runs the unlock, writes the speed selectors (SS0 `0x88888888`, which selects the full BF16 rate, and the 4-bit SS1 `0x8` IMLA4) and performs FLR before the unmodified NVIDIA driver binds the card. It is neither a UEFI application nor a patched NVIDIA driver. 

The benefit of this early kmod driver is that it does not require manual patching each time nvidia releases a new driver version.

The effect of this unlock is that it doubles the instruction issuing speed of FP/BF16 FMA into FP32 operations on GA102, GA103, GA104 and GA106 cards.

[3090 Ti dense 8192³ GEMM at 450 W, five-sample medians with FP32 accumulation](https://github.com/Zagitta/gpu-unlock/issues/1#issue-5905622687):


| Input | Before       | After         |
| ----- | ------------ | ------------- |
| FP16  | 87.46 TFLOPS | 118.39 TFLOPS |
| BF16  | 87.50 TFLOPS | 157.41 TFLOPS |
| TF32  | 42.58 TFLOPS | 82.61 TFLOPS  |

## Tested cards

Results reported by users. The module accepts every GeForce ID listed in
`kernel/gpu_unlock/main.c`, but the cards below are the ones someone has
reported on. Please add yours with a
[compatibility report](https://github.com/Zagitta/gpu-unlock/issues/new?template=compatibility-report.yml),
whether it worked or not.

| Chip  | Card                              | PCI ID      | Result                              | BF16 GEMM gain | Reports |
| ----- | --------------------------------- | ----------- | ----------------------------------- | -------------- | ------- |
| GA102 | RTX 3090 Ti                       | `10de:2203` | Unlocked                            | +68–80%        | [#1](https://github.com/Zagitta/gpu-unlock/issues/1) |
| GA102 | RTX 3090                          | `10de:2204` | Unlocked                            | +25–67%        | [#5](https://github.com/Zagitta/gpu-unlock/issues/5), [#9](https://github.com/Zagitta/gpu-unlock/issues/9), [#10](https://github.com/Zagitta/gpu-unlock/issues/10), [#17](https://github.com/Zagitta/gpu-unlock/issues/17), [#25](https://github.com/Zagitta/gpu-unlock/issues/25), [#27](https://github.com/Zagitta/gpu-unlock/issues/27), [#33](https://github.com/Zagitta/gpu-unlock/issues/33) |
| GA102 | RTX 3080 Ti 20 GB (OEM, GA102-250) | `10de:2205` | Unlock completes, BF16 stays at half rate | —        | [#28](https://github.com/Zagitta/gpu-unlock/issues/28) |
| GA102 | RTX 3080 10 GB                    | `10de:2206` | Unlocked                            | +70–73%        | [#14](https://github.com/Zagitta/gpu-unlock/issues/14) |
| GA102 | RTX 3080 20 GB (memory upgrade)   | `10de:2206` | Unlocked                            | +56–59%        | [#10](https://github.com/Zagitta/gpu-unlock/issues/10), [#15](https://github.com/Zagitta/gpu-unlock/issues/15) |
| GA104 | RTX 3070                          | `10de:2484` | Unlocked                            | +73–81%        | [#10](https://github.com/Zagitta/gpu-unlock/issues/10), [#12](https://github.com/Zagitta/gpu-unlock/issues/12) |
| GA104 | RTX 3070 Ti                       | `10de:2482` | Not tested with this module (the same unlock worked from a UEFI port on Windows) | — | [#32](https://github.com/Zagitta/gpu-unlock/issues/32) |
| GA106 | RTX 3060 12 GB                    | `10de:2504` | Unlocked                            | about +80%     | [#13](https://github.com/Zagitta/gpu-unlock/pull/13), [#31](https://github.com/Zagitta/gpu-unlock/issues/31) |
| GA103 | any                               | `10de:2414` | No reports yet                      | —              | — |

The gains are dense GEMM throughput from each report's own benchmark, so
they are not directly comparable. The power limit matters a lot: the lowest
figure (+25%) is from cards capped at 225 W.

Matrix-heavy work speeds up: LLM prefill (+14–36% in
[#9](https://github.com/Zagitta/gpu-unlock/issues/9),
[#15](https://github.com/Zagitta/gpu-unlock/issues/15),
[#25](https://github.com/Zagitta/gpu-unlock/issues/25) and
[#33](https://github.com/Zagitta/gpu-unlock/issues/33)), diffusion and
FlashAttention. LLM decode, which is limited by memory bandwidth, and INT8
work stay about the same. The reports that compared outputs found them
bit-identical before and after.

Reports also cover up to four cards in one machine, the card driving the
display, and cards passed through to a VM with vfio-pci
([#17](https://github.com/Zagitta/gpu-unlock/issues/17)).




## How to install

First run:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/Zagitta/gpu-unlock
cd gpu-unlock
make install
```

Then append `gpu_unlock.targets=all` to your kernel command line, keeping
existing options:

- **GRUB (Debian/Ubuntu/Mint):** add it inside `GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX_DEFAULT`
in `/etc/default/grub`, then run `sudo update-grub`.
- **GRUB (Arch/CachyOS):** same edit, then run
`sudo grub-mkconfig -o /boot/grub/grub.cfg`.
- **Fedora/RHEL:** run
`sudo grubby --update-kernel=ALL --args="gpu_unlock.targets=all"`.
- **systemd-boot:** append it to the `options` line in your boot entry
(`bootctl status` shows its location).
- **UKI / generated entries:** add it to `/etc/kernel/cmdline` and regenerate
your boot images/entries (e.g. `sudo mkinitcpio -P` for mkinitcpio UKIs).



## Local build

Every build downloads the pinned NVIDIA/CachyOS inputs over HTTPS, checks
their SHA-256, and generates firmware only in the build directory and the
binary package. All three formats install through the same `make install-*`
targets. Packages are built from the committed `HEAD`.

Build, install build dependencies, and install the packages in one step
(asks for your sudo password):

```sh
make install        # detect the distribution and select an installer
make install-arch   # makepkg -sif
make install-deb    # apt-get build-dep, dpkg-buildpackage, apt-get install
make install-rpm    # dnf builddep, rpmbuild, dnf install
```

`make install` uses `/etc/os-release` (`ID`, then `ID_LIKE`) to detect Arch,
Debian/Ubuntu, or Fedora/RHEL/CentOS families. The RPM installer requires DNF.
For other distributions, select a compatible explicit target above.

`make arch`, `make deb` and `make rpm` only build. Debian and RPM packages go
to `build/deb` and `build/rpm`. The NVIDIA inputs are cached in
`~/.cache/gpu-unlock/inputs` (`make inputs`; override with `INPUTS=`).
`dpkg-buildpackage` itself never uses the network, so a clean-chroot build (sbuild or
pbuilder) needs `GPU_UNLOCK_INPUTS` pointing at that cache.
The `make dist` archive, the Debian source package and the `.nosrc.rpm`
contain no NVIDIA archives or generated firmware.

## Boot flow and opt-in

The packages put `gpu_unlock` and its firmware in the initramfs and load it
there, before `nvidia` can bind a card:

- **mkinitcpio:** `/etc/mkinitcpio.conf.d/zz-gpu-unlock.conf` inserts
`gpu_unlock` right before `nvidia` in `MODULES`, so a display card is blank
for as short a time as possible. Without `nvidia` in the image, it goes
last and still runs before an `nvidia` loaded from the root filesystem.
Images are rebuilt on install. mkinitcpio ignores drop-ins for an image
built with `-c <config>` or a preset `_config`; put `gpu_unlock` right
before `nvidia` in that config's `MODULES` yourself.
- **initramfs-tools:** `/usr/share/initramfs-tools/modules.d/gpu-unlock.conf`.
- **dracut:** `/usr/lib/dracut/dracut.conf.d/gpu-unlock.conf`.

With initramfs-tools and dracut, the module is built for every installed
kernel that has headers, and those kernels' images are rebuilt on install
and again on removal. Kernels installed later get the module and a new
image from the kernel's own install hooks.

There is no `softdep nvidia pre:` rule: kmod honours only the first
`softdep nvidia` line it reads, so other packages' rules (`nvidia-utils`,
`gddr6_hwmon`) would silently override it, or it would override theirs.

The module does nothing unless the kernel command line opts in:

```
gpu_unlock.targets=all                          # every unbound GA102/GA103/GA104/GA106 card
gpu_unlock.targets=0000:21:00.0                 # only these cards
gpu_unlock.targets=0000:21:00.0,0000:22:00.0    # comma-separated
```

Addresses are full PCI names as `lspci -D` prints them (hex digits in either
case), independent of GPU numbering and display role. An entry that is not
a GA102/GA103/GA104/GA106 card, including `all` mixed with addresses, is logged and ignored.
The cards are unlocked concurrently, about a second in all however many
there are, and each on its own: a card that is already bound or powered
down is skipped. Bus mastering that the board firmware left on (Supermicro
X11 does this whatever its option ROM and bus master settings) is cleared
first; a card some driver already initialised is still refused. Then
`nvidia` loads and binds every card as usual.

The display card works too. Its firmware framebuffer (the boot console and
Plymouth) keeps running while the unlock's firmware steps run, and is
removed just before the card's reset, as `nvidia-drm` would do a moment
later anyway. Its screen is blank from that reset until `nvidia-drm` takes
over.

Loading the module by hand after boot does nothing to a card that `nvidia`
has bound.

Suspend to RAM powers the cards off, which resets the speed selectors. After
resume the module unlocks every card it unlocked at boot again, before
`nvidia` resumes it: its suspend notifier runs just ahead of the one `nvidia`
resumes its cards from (`NVreg_UseKernelSuspendNotifiers=1`, the default in
current drivers; `nvidia-resume.service` runs later still). This adds about a
second to resume. A card that kept power, as in suspend to idle, is still
unlocked and is only read. A card that `nvidia` has already resumed, or that is
bound to another driver, is left as it is, and the log says why. Add
`gpu_unlock.resume=0` to the kernel command line, or write `0` to
`/sys/module/gpu_unlock/parameters/resume`, to turn this off. Hibernation is
not covered.

Check the result with:

```sh
journalctl -k -b | grep gpu_unlock
lspci -nnk -s 0000:21:00.0
```

To stop unlocking, remove `gpu_unlock.targets=` from the kernel command line;
for a one-off boot, delete it in the bootloader's edit screen. Removing the
packages also removes the module and the initramfs drop-ins.

If the firmware on a card never stops, the module logs it and keeps the DMA
buffers that firmware may still use until the next power off. Power off
before trying again.

The kernel module and local packaging are GPL-2.0-only. The generated payload
derives from the pinned CMP reference; NVIDIA firmware remains under its own
terms. See `firmware/NOTICE.md` and `licenses/` for attribution and notices.

# REA Investigation Prompts (REAP) — Reverse Engineering with your Coding Agent

A curated collection of prompts for [REA (Reverse Engineer Anything)](https://rea.tools/) — the toolset that lets your AI coding agent inspect how software works, from native binaries, firmware and kernels to games, Electron apps, APKs and websites.

Prompts are ready to paste into your agent. Replace everything in `<angle brackets>` and keep each request focused on **one feature** — narrow questions get evidence-backed answers.

Anti-cheat, DMA, DRM, kernel and vulnerability prompts below are for **security research, interoperability, CTFs, bug bounties and testing the protection of your own software**. Bypassing protection of software you don't own, cheating in online games, or weaponizing a found vulnerability may violate law and terms of service. Every prompt asks the agent to separate *confirmed facts* from *hypotheses* and to cite evidence — treat that as non-negotiable.

## 0. Install & verify

```text

First, show me the installation plan and the configuration changes for my
approval. After the install, verify the connection and list the available
tools and workflows.
```

## 1. Getting started

### First exercise — trace a CSV export

```text
Download https://rea.tools/examples/notes-example.zip into a new folder and
extract the contents.

Use REA to investigate what happens when I click "Export notes". Trace the
flow from the button to the file write.

Show where notes.csv is created, which fields it contains, and the files and

```

### First look at an unfamiliar app

```text

three features worth investigating first. Keep it short and point to evidence
for each claim.
```

## 2. Feature tracing (any program)

### Explain one feature

```text
Use REA to investigate how <FEATURE> works in <PATH TO APPLICATION>.

Identify the entry point, the functions involved, the data flow, the
dependencies and the observable effects.

For every conclusion, present evidence: file, function, address or relevant
snippet. Separate confirmed facts, inferences and points that remain unknown.

Do not execute the application in this step.
```

### Trace a button to its effect

```text

until the result is written, sent or shown. Name every module or function on
the path and what each one does.
```

### Recover a rule and rebuild it

```text
rule in plain words, then build a minimal standalone version I can run, and
give me one input that proves it matches the original.
```

## 3. Native binary exploration

### Understand an executable

```text
Analyze <PATH TO EXECUTABLE> with REA.

Identify format, architecture, runtime, libraries, relevant strings and
possible entry points.

Map the main components and explain their responsibilities with evidence.
State which analysis engine is available and its limitations.

Start with static analysis.
```

### Function deep-dive

```text
Use REA on <binary>. Pick the function that handles <operation> and produce:
decompiled pseudocode, its callers and callees, the data structures it reads
or writes, and every string/global it touches. Annotate each finding with the
address range that proves it.
```

### Imports, strings and triage map

```text
Use REA on <binary>. Produce a triage map: file format and architecture,
section layout, linked libraries and imports grouped by capability (network,
filesystem, crypto, process/thread, registry/IPC), interesting strings with
their addresses, and the top candidate entry points for <FEATURE>. Flag any
signs of packing, obfuscation or control-flow flattening.
```

### File-format reverse engineering

```text
Use REA on <program> to work out how it reads and writes <file type>.
Describe the structure field by field, show where each field is parsed, and
write a small reader that prints a sample file.
```

### Protocol / serialization extraction

```text
Use REA on <binary> to recover the wire format used for <feature>'s network or
IPC traffic. Show the marshal/unmarshal functions with addresses, list every
field (size, endianness, encoding), and produce a Python struct/proto
definition plus one example message built from the code's constants.
```

## 4. Software & feature cloning

> Clean-room methodology: extract *behavior*, not code. Never copy
> proprietary source, assets, branding or licensing mechanisms.

### Full application clone (behavioral)

```text
Use REA to study <application> as a black box for a clean-room clone.

Produce CLONE_SPEC.md covering: every user-visible feature, screen and state
machine; inputs, outputs and edge cases; file formats and network protocols it
uses; settings and persistence layout; error behaviors.

For each requirement, cite the evidence (function, address, string, captured
request). Mark anything unconfirmed as UNKNOWN. Do not copy code or assets —
I will implement from the spec only.
```

### Clone one feature into my own app

```text
Use REA to recover the exact behavior of <FEATURE> in <application>: trigger,
inputs, processing steps, outputs, side effects and failure modes.

Then implement <FEATURE> from scratch in <MY LANGUAGE/PROJECT> matching that
behavior, with tests derived from the recovered rules. List every observable
difference that remains between my version and the original.
```

### Validate a clone against the original

```text
Compare <MY IMPLEMENTATION> with the observed behavior of <ORIGINAL
APPLICATION>.

Use verify_reconstruction, if available. Check results, errors, limits and
state transitions.

Present passing cases, divergences and behaviors not yet tested. Do not
consider equivalence demonstrated just because a few examples passed.
```

### UI/UX behavior cloning without assets

```text
Use REA on <application> to document its interaction model: layout logic,
keyboard shortcuts, command dispatch, undo/redo semantics and clipboard
formats. Recreate the behavior in <my framework> using only my own visual
assets, matching the documented semantics. Show which original function
proves each documented rule.
```

---

## 5. Games

### Gameplay logic recovery

```text
Use REA to reconstruct <GAME> from its executable. Recover the gameplay logic
in C and test it against the original.

For each mechanic (movement, physics, scoring, spawning), show the function,
the constants and the update loop that prove the rule.
```

### Speed / difficulty rule (dino-style)

```text
Use REA to inspect <game>. Why does <difficulty/speed> change over time? Show
the exact rule and the constants behind it, then build a small standalone
version with an adjustable parameter.
```

### Engine & asset pipeline map

```text
Use REA on <game executable/data folder>. Identify the engine or framework,
the render loop, the update/tick order, how levels and assets are loaded and
serialized, and where gameplay data lives (tables, scripts, archives). Map
each component to functions/addresses and describe the load pipeline step by
step.
```

### Single-player mod support (offline only)

```text
Use REA on <offline single-player game> to locate the code that controls
<weapon stats / spawn rates / economy>. Show the data tables or functions with
addresses. I only want to understand where the values live so I can build my
own offline trainer for personal experimentation — no multiplayer, no
persistence tricks.
```

---

## 6. Game portability to WASM

### Port a native game to the browser

```text
Use REA to analyze <game executable/source> as a portability target for WASM.

Map: the main loop and frame pacing, the rendering backend (OpenGL/DirectX/
SDL/Vulkan calls), filesystem and save paths, threading model, audio output,
input handling, and any platform-specific APIs or inline assembly.

For each, classify as: portable as-is / needs shim / must be rewritten. Cite
the functions and call sites that prove each classification.
```

### Build the port plan

```text
Based on the REA findings for <game>, produce a WASM port plan:
- toolchain choice (Emscripten or manual recompile) and required shims
  (GL→WebGL, SDL→SDL2-compat, pthreads→SharedArrayBuffer/threads);
- the minimal set of source modules to compile;
- how saves move to IndexedDB and assets to fetch/streaming;
- performance risks found in the native code (allocation per frame, busy
  loops, 64-bit assumptions) with function evidence;
- a milestone list ending in a playable index.html.
```

### Port the logic core first (headless)

```text
Use REA to isolate <game>'s pure simulation logic (physics, AI, rules) from
rendering and OS calls. Extract the exact rules with evidence, then implement
that logic core in C/Rust compiled to WASM with a test harness that replays
recorded inputs and compares state hashes against the original behavior.
```

---

## 7. Firmware & embedded

### Firmware image triage

```text
Use REA to analyze <firmware image / bin / img>.

Identify the container format, extract partitions/filesystems (JFFS2, SquashFS,
UBI, cramfs...), map each region to architecture and load address, locate the
kernel and rootfs, and list boot entries, init scripts and services.

Show offsets, entropy observations and the evidence for every claim. Start
with static analysis; do not flash or run anything.
```

### MCU / IoT binary analysis

```text
Use REA on <firmware blob> for a <ARM Cortex-M / MIPS / AVR / ESP32> target.

Find the vector table and reset handler, reconstruct the memory map from
literal pools and peripheral base addresses, identify the RTOS (FreeRTOS,
Zephyr...) from symbol/string fingerprints, and map the main task loop and
peripheral drivers (UART, SPI, I2C, radio stack) with function addresses.
```

### Embedded protocol & update mechanism

```text
Use REA on <firmware> to recover: the network stack usage (hardcoded IPs,
DNS, MQTT/HTTP endpoints, ports), the OTA update path (download URL, signature
check, flash write), and credential material (keys, default passwords, debug
tokens). For each finding give the function/address and say whether the
behavior is confirmed statically or still a hypothesis.
```

---

## 8. Android

### Audit an APK

```text
Use REA to analyze <PATH TO APK>.

List declared permissions, exported components, analytics/tracking SDKs,
domains found and local storage mechanisms.

For each finding, show the corresponding class, method or file.

Distinguish references present in the code from behaviors actually observed.
Do not conclude that a domain is accessed just because it appears in a string.
```

### Trace a feature through Java/Kotlin and native code

```text
Use REA on <APK> to trace <FEATURE> end to end: UI entry point (Activity/
Fragment/Composable), the Java/Kotlin call chain, any JNI boundaries
(RegisterNatives / native library loads), the .so functions involved, and the
final effect (network call, file write, database row). Show class, method and
offset evidence at every hop.
```

### Storage, crypto and secrets review

```text
Use REA on <APK>. Determine how the app stores <data>: SharedPreferences,
SQLite, files, keystore. Recover any embedded crypto (hardcoded keys/IVs,
obfuscation routines) with the class/method that uses them. State whether
data is encrypted at rest and in transit, with evidence, and list concrete
risks.
```

### Obfuscated / packed app triage

```text
Use REA on <APK> that appears obfuscated or packed. Identify the packer or
protector (string/class fingerprints, loader stub in the native libs), map
what is statically visible vs. deferred to runtime, and propose the minimal
safe steps to reach the real dex/native code for analysis.
```

---

## 9. Kernel analysis

### Driver inspection (Windows / Linux)

```text
Use REA on <driver binary: .sys / .ko>.

Identify the format and target OS version, the entry/init routine, the device
object and driver dispatch table, every IOCTL code with its input/output
buffer validation, the callbacks/notifications it registers, and the memory it
reads or writes outside its own allocations.

Map each finding to function/address evidence. Static analysis only — do not
load the driver.
```

### IOCTL attack-surface enumeration

```text
Use REA on <driver>. Enumerate all control codes handled, and for each:
the handler function, how it validates input/output buffers (probe methods,
size checks, IRQL assumptions), and any copy_to_user/copy_from_user or
memcpy with attacker-controlled length. Rank the handlers by risk with
evidence for the ranking.
```

### Kernel subsystem / syscall behavior

```text
Use REA on <kernel binary or module> to explain how <subsystem/syscall>
processes <input>. Trace from the syscall/dispatch entry to the parsing
functions, show bounds checks (or their absence), the data structures
populated, and error paths. Cite addresses for each step.
```

---

## 10. Vulnerability research

### Trust-boundary audit

```text
Use REA to review the security of <authorized application or binary>.

Prioritize trust boundaries, untrusted input, privileged operations,
credential storage, IPC, file handling and command execution.

For each possible vulnerability, present:
- the input origin and the sensitive operation;
- the code path and existing checks;
- preconditions and impact;
- evidence and uncertainties;
- a proposal for controlled validation.

Do not classify a hypothesis as a confirmed vulnerability without sufficient
evidence.
```

### Sink hunt from untrusted input

```text
Use REA on <binary>. List every place untrusted data enters (network sockets,
files, IPC, command-line, clipboard, URL handlers) and follow each source to
dangerous sinks: memcpy/strcpy with unchecked length, system/exec, dynamic
loading, deserialization, path concatenation. For each source→sink path give
the function chain with addresses and state which validation exists in
between.
```

### Patch diffing (1-day to incomplete-fix hunting)

```text
Use REA to compare <vulnerable version> and <patched version> of <component>.

Diff the security-relevant functions: what check was added, where else in the
binary the same pattern exists without the fix, and whether the fix covers
every caller of the vulnerable routine. Report candidate incomplete-fix
locations with function/address evidence, clearly labeled as hypotheses until
validated in a controlled environment.
```

### Crash triage to root cause

```text
Use REA to investigate this crash in <application>.

Available evidence:
<STACK TRACE, LOGS, DUMP OR REPRO STEPS>

Relate the error to the functions involved, formulate hypotheses and indicate
which evidence supports each one.

Propose the smallest experiment needed to distinguish the hypotheses and
validate the cause.
```

### How is my data handled?

```text
I am allowed to analyse <program>. Use REA to find where it stores or sends
<kind of data>. Show the code paths, say whether the data is encrypted at rest
and in transit, and list concrete risks with evidence.
```

---

## 11. Electron & JavaScript

### Electron app anatomy

```text
Use REA to analyze <PATH TO ELECTRON APP>.

Locate the JavaScript files and any app.asar archives. Map the main and
renderer processes, the preload scripts and the IPC channels.

Then trace <FEATURE> from the UI to its implementation, including network
calls and filesystem operations. Show the evidence.
```

### IPC & contextIsolation security review

```text
Use REA on <Electron app>. Enumerate every ipcMain handler and the channels
exposed via contextBridge/preload. For each channel: what arguments it
accepts, whether it reaches shell.openExternal, child_process, fs, or webview
navigation, and what validation exists. Flag any handler where renderer-
controlled input reaches a privileged sink without checks — with file and
function evidence.
```

### Minified / bundled JS feature tracing

```text
Use REA on <app.asar / bundle.js> to trace <FEATURE> through minified code.
Identify the module boundaries, recover the relevant functions with readable
names, follow the data flow from the UI event to the network/filesystem
effect, and produce a call graph. Cite offsets in the bundle for each hop.
```

### Web feature mapping

```text
Use REA to observe <site> while I use <feature>. List the requests, scripts
and state changes involved, then summarise how the feature works and which
parts run on the client versus the server.
```

### Website clone (structure + behavior)

```text
Use REA to inspect https://<site>/. Recover the page structure, the client
routes, the API calls each view makes and the state management pattern.
Rebuild a functional equivalent with my own assets and styling, matching the
observed behavior. List requests and scripts as evidence per view.
```

---

## 12. Anti-cheat & protection research

> Scope these at **your own machine, your own software, a vendor bug bounty,
> a CTF, or academic study**. Never at other players' live game sessions.

### Map an anti-cheat's detection surface

```text
Use REA to analyze <anti-cheat driver/service binary> on a lab machine I own.

Identify: what it enumerates (processes, modules, handles, callbacks), which
integrity checks it performs, what it hooks or registers with the kernel, and
what data it sends out (endpoints, intervals, payload fields).

For each finding cite the function/address. Separate "code present" from
"behavior observed". Do not run the target game; static analysis first.
```

### Test my own product's protections

```text
I own <my application> and its protection scheme. Use REA to assess it as an
attacker would: locate the license check, the integrity checks, the
anti-debug/anti-VM tricks, and trace what a failed check does. Report which
checks are trivially bypassable, which are load-bearing, and concrete fixes —
each claim backed by file/function/address evidence.
```

### DRM / license flow analysis (interoperability)

```text
Use REA on <application> to document its licensing flow: where entitlement is
validated, what local and remote checks exist, what state is stored on disk,
and how offline mode behaves. Goal is interoperability and security review of
software I legitimately own. Report facts with evidence; flag anything you
could not confirm.
```

---

## 13. DMA & hardware-assisted cheat research (defensive)

> DMA attacks are a real anti-cheat and platform-security problem. Use these
> to **study how detection works** and to **harden your own product/lab** —
> on machines you own, offline targets, or with vendor authorization. Reading
> another machine's memory over PCIe without authorization is illegal in most
> jurisdictions.

### How DMA memory access works on a target platform

```text
Use REA on <anti-cheat driver / DMA-protection firmware (e.g. Thunderbolt
security, IOMMU/VT-d config)> in my lab.

Explain, with function/address evidence: how the platform restricts external
PCIe memory reads (IOMMU mappings, Thunderbolt ACLs, kernel DMA protection),
what the anti-cheat enumerates to spot a DMA device (PCIe topology, BAR
regions, unknown root ports, timing anomalies), and which checks are
load-bearing versus cosmetic.
```

### Analyze a DMA-cheat toolchain sample (malware-style)

```text
I have a sample <DMA firmware / PCILeech-style driver / user-mode reader> for
defensive research. Use REA to document: how it opens physical memory
(XNVIPHYSTREE-style access, PCIe BAR mapping), how it locates the game process
(PEB walking, page-table traversal), what it reads/writes, and any
anti-detection tricks (pattern scanning avoidance, timing padding). Give the
function chain with addresses for each stage. Do not run it against any live
game — analysis only.
```

### Detection-gap analysis for my own product

```text
Use REA to evaluate how <my application/my anti-cheat component> would react
to external physical memory access: which integrity checks exist, whether
sensitive values sit in predictable memory, what side-channel validation the
server performs. Propose concrete hardening (value obfuscation, server-side
validation, memory layout randomization) mapped to the code locations that
need each change.
```

### FPGA/microcontroller device firmware study

```text
Use REA on <device firmware dump> from a PCIe/USB device I own. Identify the
MCU/FPGA soft-core, the protocol it speaks to the host, the memory-read
primitives it implements, and how it hides from host enumeration. Show
evidence per claim and label anything that needs runtime confirmation.
```

---

## 14. Software cracking research

> For studying protection schemes, crackmes/CTFs, malware-adjacent RE, and
> hardening your own software. Not a guide to pirate other people's products.

### Keygen-repair style analysis (document, don't bypass)

```text
Use REA on <binary> to find the validation routine for <license key / serial>.
Recover the algorithm (decompile it), identify the input encoding, the
checksum/transform steps and the success/failure branches with addresses.
Then write a test harness that exercises the recovered algorithm against
sample inputs. Do not patch or bypass anything — I want the algorithm
documented, not the check removed.
```

### Crackme / CTF challenge solving

```text
Use REA on this crackme: <path>. Enumerate entry points, strings, imports and
any packer/protection indicators. Identify the flag-checking logic, decompile
it, and derive the correct input from the recovered algorithm. Show the full
evidence chain: address → instruction → conclusion.
```

### Protection-diffing between versions

```text
Use REA to compare <protected app v1> and <v2>. Identify what changed in the
protection layer: new integrity checks, new anti-debug tricks, changed
validation paths. Map each change to functions/addresses and explain the
hardening intent.
```

---

## 15. Version comparison & crash work

### Compare two versions

```text
Use the compare_application_versions workflow, if available, to compare
<OLD VERSION> and <NEW VERSION> of <application>.

Identify functional changes, API changes, dependency and permission changes,
and possible security fixes.

Map each change to the corresponding functions or files and explain the
impact. Differentiate build changes from behavior changes.
```

---

## 16. Long-running investigations

### Continue where you left off

```text
Review the evidence and notes of this investigation.

Use audit_residual_unknowns, if available, to list what has not been
demonstrated yet.

Prioritize the next analyses by how much they can reduce uncertainty. Update
an INVESTIGATION.md file with findings, evidence, discarded hypotheses and
next steps.
```

---

## Wildcard prompt (start here)

```text
Use REA to understand how <FEATURE> works in <PATH TO APPLICATION>.

Check first which tools are actually available. Start with static analysis
and trace the feature down to the responsible functions.

Present evidence for each conclusion, separate facts from hypotheses, and
record the limitations. At the end, generate a behavioral specification and
propose tests to verify it.
```

---

## Prompt-writing tips (why these work)

1. **One feature per prompt.** Broad "explain the whole app" questions return shallow maps; narrow ones return call chains and addresses.
2. **Demand evidence.** Every prompt here requires file/function/address citations — it stops the agent from confabulating.
3. **Separate fact / inference / unknown.** The three-bucket format keeps hypotheses honest.
4. **Static first.** Say "do not execute the application" until you actually need runtime observation.
5. **End with a deliverable.** SPEC.md, a reader script, a port plan, a minimal rebuild — a concrete artifact forces the agent to verify its own claims.
6. **State the scope out loud.** "Lab machine I own", "offline single-player", "document, don't bypass" — the framing keeps results usable for research and reporting.

## Next steps: see what people built with REA

Ran one of these prompts? See what others are doing with REA at **[madewithrea.com](https://madewithrea.com)**, a community directory of REA investigations, rebuilds, integrations and tools, sorted by use case (native binaries, Android, games, firmware, Electron and more).

items.readme:
# IPA decryptor

Decrypt FairPlay-encrypted apps using a 16-byte credential
for the account that owns each IPA. [Credential retrieval](credential-retrieval/README.md)
gets it from a supported jailbroken device and writes
`credential.bin` to the chosen output directory.

Decryption runs on macOS and Linux.

Supports version-3 and version-5 SUPF, 448-byte and 440-byte SINF `priv`
records, and encrypted arm64 Mach-O slices. A 440-byte record must end in
eight zero bytes.

## Set up

From this directory, with Python 3.9+ and a C compiler:

```sh
python3 -m venv .venv
. .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
make
```

On macOS, `make` also builds the credential-retrieval bundle and requires
Xcode and `ldid`. On Linux, it builds the decryptor.

## Decrypt

```sh
python decrypt.py /path/to/encrypted.ipa /path/to/decrypted.ipa \
  --credential /path/to/credential.bin
```

If `--credential` is omitted, the tool reads `./credential.bin`. The output
path must not exist.

The decryptor uses each IPA's SINF and SUPF records to derive page keys,
decrypt its encrypted arm64 pages, and clear `cryptid`.

items.readme:
php2shell

CVE-2026-109618 & CVE-2026-109619 — Independent Research & Verification

--- Two critical pre-authentication RCE vulnerabilities in PHP core, exploiting `session.upload_progress` (enabled by default) and the memory allocator's OOM bailout. **14 years of vulnerable code** (PHP 5.4.0, 2012 — present). **Author:** [Qi Deng](https://github.com/ikow)  |  **Writeup:** [qideng.substack.com](https://qideng.substack.com/p/php2shell-dissecting-phps-critical)  |  **Date:** 2026-10-21 ## Impact | What | Scale | |------|-------| | Websites running PHP | **78%** of all websites | | WordPress alone | **43%** of all websites | | Affected versions | PHP 5.4.0 through 8.5.11 (14 years) | | Authentication required | **None** | | Application vulnerability required | **None** (Chain D — mod_php) | ## Verified Attack Chains ### Chain A — Session File Injection + LFI → RCE Upload a file with PHP code in the filename → `session.upload_progress` stores it raw in the session file → include via any LFI → code execution. ``` Conditions: upload_progress=On (default) + application has LFI Reliability: 100% ``` ### Chain B — var_destroy UAF → Handler Overwrite → RCE `var_destroy()` frees back-reference chunks then fires `__destruct` without `serialize_lock`. Inner `unserialize()` reuses the freed var_hash → heap-use-after-free → overwrite function handler → RCE. ``` Conditions: application calls unserialize() with controlled data ASAN: heap-use-after-free CONFIRMED at var_unserializer.c:851 ``` ### Chain C — Session Handler Mismatch → `__destruct` → RCE Session written with `php_serialize` handler (pipe `|` preserved in filename) → read by `php` handler → splits at `|` → deserializes injected object → `__destruct` fires during var_hash cleanup **even when decode returns FAILURE**. ``` Conditions: two directories with different session.serialize_handler Key finding: __destruct fires on BOTH success and failure paths ``` ### Chain D — mod_php OOM → Stale EG() → RCE ⚡ Multipart POST triggers OOM during request startup → `longjmp()` skips `init_executor` → Apache mod_php runs shutdown on stale `EG()` globals → use-after-free → RCE. ``` Conditions: NONE — any PHP endpoint on Apache mod_php SAPI: Apache mod_php ✅ | FPM ⚠️ (child exits) | FrankenPHP ✅ ``` **This is a pre-auth, zero-dependency RCE against default Apache mod_php installations.** ### Chain E — FPM Session OOM → Stale BG(unserialize) → RCE ⚡ Producer request: `session_start()` decodes ~30MB session → OOM during `php_var_unserialize` → `BG(unserialize).level` stays >0, session destruction state dirty → FPM worker **survives**. Consumer request: `upload_progress` triggers `rfc1867` handler (runs **before** `PHP_RINIT_FUNCTION(basic)`) → accesses stale `BG(unserialize)` → "Session object destruction failed" → `__destruct` on stale objects → UAF → RCE. ``` Conditions: session_start() endpoint + large session file + FPM Key finding: rfc1867 runs BEFORE basic_rinit — stale BG(unserialize) is accessible Verified: "Session object destruction failed" during PHP Request Startup ``` ## Official CVE Details | CVE | GHSA | Description | |-----|------|-------------| | CVE-2026-109618 | [GHSA-w8hw-w9fx-j79w](https://github.com/php/php-src/security/advisories/GHSA-w8hw-w9fx-j79w) | RCE via OOM corruption — `longjmp()` leaves request state invalid | | CVE-2026-109619 | [GHSA-6wmf-4rv5-p3rp](https://github.com/php/php-src/security/advisories/GHSA-6wmf-4rv5-p3rp) | RCE via stale global state — worker retains freed request memory | **Patch:** [Commit 3584a98](https://github.com/php/php-src/commit/3584a98bda) — 300 files changed, replaces `longjmp()` with delayed soft OOM + hard `_exit()`. ## Quick Start ```bash # Clone git clone https://github.com/ikow/php2shell-poc.git && cd php2shell-poc # Start lab (PHP-FPM + nginx + Apache mod_php) cd lab && docker compose up -d # Verify Chain A: Session injection python3 ../poc/verify_session_injection.py --target http://127.0.0.1:18080 # Verify Chain B: UAF (requires ASAN build) USE_ZEND_ALLOC=0 ASAN_OPTIONS="detect_leaks=0" php ../poc/verify_uaf_asan.php # Verify Chain C: Handler mismatch python3 ../poc/verify_handler_mismatch.py --target http://127.0.0.1:18080 # Verify Chain D: OOM on Apache mod_php python3 ../poc/verify_oom_trigger.py --host 127.0.0.1 --port 18081 --strategy headers # Verify Chain E: FPM stale BG state python3 ../poc/verify_fpm_stale_state.py --target http://127.0.0.1:18080 ``` ## Repository Structure ``` php2shell-poc/ ├── README.md ├── poc/ │ ├── verify_session_injection.py # Chain A: session file injection │ ├── verify_uaf_asan.php # Chain B: var_destroy UAF (ASAN) │ ├── verify_handler_mismatch.py # Chain C: handler mismatch │ ├── verify_oom_trigger.py # Chain D: OOM trigger strategies │ └── verify_fpm_stale_state.py # Chain E: FPM stale BG verification ├── lab/ │ ├── docker-compose.yml # FPM + nginx + Apache mod_php │ ├── setup.sh # One-click lab setup │ ├── php.ini # FPM configuration │ └── php-apache.ini # Apache mod_php (low memory for OOM) └── docs/ ├── ANALYSIS.md # Full technical analysis └── cover.png # Cover image ``` ## Mitigation ```ini ; Immediate — reduces attack surface but does NOT fix all chains session.upload_progress.enabled = Off session.use_only_cookies = On ``` | Mitigation | Chains blocked | |-----------|---------------| | `session.upload_progress.enabled = Off` | A, C, E (partial) | | `session.use_only_cookies = On` | A, C (session fixation) | | `memory_limit` + `post_max_size` tuning | D (reduces OOM surface) | | Update to PHP 8.2.35+ | **All chains** | > **The only complete fix is patching PHP.** The OOM corruption (Chain D) is in the Zend engine core, not in session handling. ## Timeline | Date | Event | |------|-------| | 2012-03-01 | `session.upload_progress` introduced in PHP 5.4.0 | | 2026-10-20 | Details leaked before embargo; PHP advances release | | 2026-10-21 | PHP 8.2.35 / 8.3.36 / 8.4.27 / 8.5.12 released | | 2026-10-21 | This research published | ## References - [PHP Security Advisory](https://www.php.net/archive/2026.php) - [GHSA-w8hw-w9fx-j79w](https://github.com/php/php-src/security/advisories/GHSA-w8hw-w9fx-j79w) — CVE-2026-109618 - [GHSA-6wmf-4rv5-p3rp](https://github.com/php/php-src/security/advisories/GHSA-6wmf-4rv5-p3rp) — CVE-2026-109619 - [Patch commit](https://github.com/php/php-src/commit/3584a98bda) — 300 files, Zend engine + extensions - [PR #22113](https://github.com/php/php-src/pull/22113) — Session fixation fix - [BleepingComputer coverage](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/php-ships-emergency-patches-for-critical-php2shell-flaws/) ##
