items.description: Extract huge archives in place: the archive shrinks as your files hatch, so you only need room for the output. ZIP, 7z, tar, split archives.
items.readme:
HatchZip

Extract huge archives in place. The archive shrinks as your files hatch,
so you only need free space for the output, not for the output and the archive.

Installation | Usage | Safety | How it works | Contributing

A 180 GB game download that unpacks to 200 GB needs 380 GB of disk with WinRAR, 7-Zip or `unzip`, because the archive and everything extracted from it have to exist at the same time. HatchZip needs a little over 200 GB. It extracts the archive from the end and cuts each finished part off the archive file as it goes, so the space the archive gives back is reused for the next files. It checks that the extraction will fit before it changes anything, keeps a safety margin of free space the whole way through, and can be stopped or crash at any moment and pick up where it left off. It reads ZIP, 7z, tar, `.tar.gz`, RAR volume sets and split archives. ### Get it > [!IMPORTANT] > HatchZip is only distributed from this repository's [releases](https://github.com/xevrion/hatchzip/releases) and its site, [hatchzip.dev](https://hatchzip.dev). Other sites using the name, such as hatchzip.com, are not affiliated with this project. No coding needed. **[Download for Windows](https://github.com/xevrion/hatchzip/releases/latest/download/HatchZip-x64-setup.exe)** (Windows 10 and 11), or for [macOS (Apple Silicon)](https://github.com/xevrion/hatchzip/releases/latest/download/HatchZip-aarch64.dmg), [macOS (Intel)](https://github.com/xevrion/hatchzip/releases/latest/download/HatchZip-x86_64.dmg) and [Linux](#installation). 1. Run the installer. Windows may show "Windows protected your PC" because HatchZip is not code-signed yet: choose **More info**, then **Run anyway**. 2. Right-click the archive, choose **HatchZip**, then **Extract here**. On Windows 11 the menu is under **Show more options**. 3. Or open HatchZip from the Start menu, open the archive, and choose **Extract**. HatchZip shows whether the files will fit before it changes anything. The archive is used up as the files come out, so when it finishes, only the extracted files are left. To keep the archive when there is room for both, choose **Extract here (keep archive)** in the right-click menu, or clear **Remove the archive during extraction** in the app. That is a normal extraction: the archive is not changed, and space is required for all extracted files. ## Highlights The same 200 MB of game data (21 files), packed by the real tools, extracted on a 220 MiB disk with about 50 MB free: | Archive | `unzip` / 7-Zip | HatchZip | |---|---|---| | ZIP, 180 MB | `unzip` ran out of space at file 6 of 21 | Finished, every file byte-identical | | 7z from 7-Zip 25.01, `-ms=20m` (10 solid blocks) | Needs 380 MB | Finished in 0.64 s, every file byte-identical | | 7z split into 5 volumes of 40 MB | Needs 380 MB | Finished; volumes deleted one at a time, peak 210 MB used | | tar from GNU tar, 200 MB | Needs 400 MB | Finished in 0.12 s, every file byte-identical | | 7z from 7-Zip with default settings (1 solid block) | Needs 380 MB | Refused before touching anything: one solid block can't be freed until all of it is out, so it needs 200 MB free | | | Result | |---|---| | ZIP extraction speed, same data | 0.25 to 0.35 s, against 1.48 to 1.50 s for `unzip` 6.00, including an fsync `unzip` skips | | Crash safety | Killed at both unsafe moments of a batch at many points of each format's run; every resume finished with identical output | | Works on | Any filesystem that can shrink a file: ext4, btrfs, XFS, NTFS, APFS, and also exFAT and FAT32 USB drives | Measured on Fedora 43, Intel Core i7-14700HX, SK Hynix NVMe SSD, warm page cache; the disk-space runs used a 220 MiB tmpfs to stand in for a full laptop disk, the speed runs ext4. Speed comes from decompressing files in parallel, so an archive holding one giant file extracts at the speed of a single core. The extra space HatchZip needs beyond the output is about the size of the largest single unit it can free at once: one file for ZIP and tar, one solid block for 7z. On filesystems that can punch holes (ext4, XFS, btrfs, tmpfs; NTFS and APFS not yet verified), a large file stored or deflated in a ZIP, or in a tar, frees its archive bytes every 256 MiB while it is extracted: a ZIP holding one 600 MiB stored file extracted on a 950 MiB tmpfs with 367 MB free, where it needed 629 MB before. `hatchzip check` computes the exact figure for any archive. ## Installation ### Desktop app Download from the [latest release](https://github.com/xevrion/hatchzip/releases/latest): | System | File | |---|---| | Windows 10 and 11 (x64) | [`HatchZip-x64-setup.exe`](https://github.com/xevrion/hatchzip/releases/latest/download/HatchZip-x64-setup.exe): installs per user, no admin rights, adds the right-click menu | | macOS, Apple Silicon | [`HatchZip-aarch64.dmg`](https://github.com/xevrion/hatchzip/releases/latest/download/HatchZip-aarch64.dmg) | | macOS, Intel | [`HatchZip-x86_64.dmg`](https://github.com/xevrion/hatchzip/releases/latest/download/HatchZip-x86_64.dmg) | | Debian, Ubuntu | [`hatchzip_amd64.deb`](https://github.com/xevrion/hatchzip/releases/latest/download/hatchzip_amd64.deb) | | Fedora, openSUSE | [`hatchzip-x86_64.rpm`](https://github.com/xevrion/hatchzip/releases/latest/download/hatchzip-x86_64.rpm) | | Any Linux | [`HatchZip-x86_64.AppImage`](https://github.com/xevrion/hatchzip/releases/latest/download/HatchZip-x86_64.AppImage) | The installers also put the `hatchzip` command (and its short name `hz`) on your `PATH`. The Windows setup and the macOS apps are not code-signed yet: on Windows choose **More info**, then **Run anyway**; on macOS 15 and later, open the app once, then allow it under System Settings, Privacy & Security. ### Command line only Linux and macOS: ```sh curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xevrion/hatchzip/main/install.sh | sh ``` Windows, in PowerShell: ```powershell irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xevrion/hatchzip/main/install.ps1 | iex ``` Both download the build for your machine from the latest release, check it against its published SHA-256 checksum, and install `hatchzip` and `hz` for your user only, with the man page and shell completions. No root or administrator rights. Every release file from 0.1.3 on carries signed build provenance. To check that a download really was built from this repository by its release workflow, wherever you got it: ```sh gh attestation verify HatchZip-x64-setup.exe --repo xevrion/hatchzip ``` ### Package managers Homebrew and Scoop are live. winget is in review, and the AUR packages are coming soon; until they are listed as live here, a package under those names does not come from this project. | System | Command | Installs | |---|---|---| | Arch Linux (AUR) | `yay -S hatchzip-bin`, or `yay -S hatchzip` to build from source | App and CLI | | Windows (winget) | `winget install Xevrion.HatchZip` | App and CLI, same as the setup | | Windows (Scoop) | `scoop bucket add xevrion https://github.com/xevrion/scoop-bucket`, then `scoop install xevrion/hatchzip` | CLI | | macOS and Linux (Homebrew) | `brew install xevrion/tap/hatchzip` | CLI | | macOS (Homebrew) | `brew install --cask xevrion/tap/hatchzip` | App and CLI | ### With Cargo ```sh cargo install hatchzip ``` This builds the command line tool from [crates.io](https://crates.io/crates/hatchzip). The engine is a library too: [`hatchzip-core`](https://crates.io/crates/hatchzip-core). It reads every format but RAR; `cargo install hatchzip --features rar` adds RAR support, which compiles UnRAR's C++ source under its own [license](#license) and needs a C++ compiler. ### From source With [Rust](https://rustup.rs) (the version is pinned in `rust-toolchain.toml` and installed automatically): ```sh git clone https://github.com/xevrion/hatchzip.git cd hatchzip cargo build --release ``` The binaries are `target/release/hatchzip` and `target/release/hatchzip-gui` (`.exe` on Windows). Building the desktop app on Linux needs the fontconfig headers (`libfontconfig1-dev` or `fontconfig-devel`). `cargo build --release --features rar` adds RAR support, as in the release builds; it needs a C++ compiler. ### Shell completions and man page ```sh hatchzip completions bash > ~/.local/share/bash-completion/completions/hatchzip hatchzip completions zsh > "${fpath[1]}/_hatchzip" hatchzip completions fish > ~/.config/fish/completions/hatchzip.fish hatchzip completions powershell >> $PROFILE hatchzip man > ~/.local/share/man/man1/hatchzip.1 # then: man hatchzip ``` ## Usage ### See whether it fits ```sh hatchzip check game.zip ``` ``` game.zip 180.2 MB zip, 200.0 MB uncompressed in 22 entries available 50.5 MB standard extraction needs 200.0 MB required 29.9 MB (+5.0 MB reserved) available after 30.6 MB ``` `check` reads the archive's index and the disk's free space and changes nothing. "Standard extraction needs" is what extracting while keeping the archive requires; when that fits too, `check` says so. `hatchzip check game.zip --keep-archive` shows the plan for keeping it. ### Extract ```sh hatchzip extract game.zip # into ./game/ hatchzip extract game.zip -o D:\Games\Foo # somewhere else hatchzip x game.7z.001 # split archive; any part's name works ``` HatchZip prints the same space plan, asks for confirmation, then extracts. When the extraction is complete, the archive has been removed and the files are in the output folder. For a split archive, each volume is deleted as soon as everything in it is extracted. | Option | Effect | |---|---| | `-o, --output ` | Output folder. Defaults to a folder named after the archive, next to it. It may hold other files, but none where the archive's files go. | | `--keep-archive` | Keep the archive: a normal extraction that removes nothing. Space is required for all extracted files. No confirmation is asked. | | `--keep-free ` | Free space HatchZip never uses, such as `500MB` or `10GB`. Default `2GB`, so the disk never fills to zero. | | `--verify-first` | Read the whole archive and check every file's checksum before deleting anything. Takes extra time, recommended for downloads you can't easily get again. | | `-y, --yes` | Skip the confirmation prompt. Required when not run from a terminal, unless `--keep-archive` is given. | | `-q, --quiet` | Print only errors and prompts. | ### Keep the archive ```sh hatchzip extract game.zip --keep-archive ``` When the disk has room for the archive and all its files, `--keep-archive` extracts like any other tool and leaves the archive byte for byte as it was, for when it is needed again. The space check, path and collision checks, checksums and password handling are the same as for an extraction in place. If keeping the archive does not fit, HatchZip says so, by how much, and what extracting in place would require instead. An interrupted run resumes like any other, and goes on keeping the archive even when resumed without `--keep-archive`. An extraction that started in place cannot switch to keeping the archive, since part of it is already removed. `hatchzip restore` on an archive being kept only discards the progress: the archive was never changed. ### Several archives ```sh hatchzip extract a.zip b.7z c.tar.gz ``` The archives are extracted one after another, each into its own folder, or all into the folder given with `-o`. The space for each one is checked just before it starts, so the space one archive frees is available to the next. The first archive that does not complete stops the run, and HatchZip lists which archives were extracted, which one stopped and whether its progress is saved, and which were not started; the exit status is that archive's. `check`, `test` and `list` also take several archives, go through all of them, and exit with the status of the first one that did not succeed. Naming every volume of a split archive, as a shell pattern like `game.7z.*` does, counts as that archive once. ### Stop and resume Press `Ctrl+C` and HatchZip finishes the files it is writing, saves its progress and exits. A second `Ctrl+C` quits immediately, which is also safe. To continue, run the same command again: ```sh hatchzip extract game.zip ``` The same applies after a crash, a power cut, or running out of space because something else filled the disk. Progress lives in two small files next to the archive, `game.zip.hatchzip` and `game.zip.hatchzip-tail`. **Do not delete them while an extraction is unfinished**: they hold the archive's index, which is no longer inside the archive itself. ### Stop for good To give up on an unfinished extraction instead, restore the archive: ```sh hatchzip restore game.zip ``` What is left of the archive becomes a normal archive again, holding exactly the entries not yet extracted, which 7-Zip, WinRAR, `unzip` or `tar` open as usual. The files already extracted stay in the output folder. Restore only appends a new index, so it needs only the free space that index takes, and if it is interrupted, running it again finishes it. ### List and test ```sh hatchzip list game.7z # what's inside, with sizes hatchzip test game.7z # read every file and verify its checksum, writing nothing ``` Plain tar has no checksums for file contents, so `test` on a tar only proves every file can be read in full. ### Exit status | Code | Meaning | |---|---| | 0 | Success | | 1 | Failure. If extraction had started, progress is saved. | | 2 | Invalid command line | | 3 | Not enough free space. Nothing was changed. | | 4 | The archive is damaged. Nothing was deleted. | | 5 | The archive is password protected and no correct password was given. | | 130 | Paused with Ctrl+C. Run the same command to continue. | With several archives, the status is that of the first archive that did not succeed. ## Is it safe HatchZip destroys the archive as it extracts, so it is built around never losing a file that has not safely landed on disk. - **Nothing changes until the plan fits.** The space check runs before the first byte is touched, and it replays the whole extraction to find the moment that needs the most free space, not just the total. - **A file is written, flushed to the physical disk and renamed into place before the part of the archive holding it is cut off.** A crash at any point leaves either the file or its bytes in the archive, never neither. - **Damage stops the run where it is.** Every file's CRC-32 is checked as it is extracted. A damaged file is not written, and it stays in the archive along with everything before it. - **Hostile archives are refused before anything is deleted:** paths that escape the output folder, entries that overlap each other, entries that appear twice, and links where other entries need a folder. Setuid and setgid bits are never restored, and symlinks are created only after every regular file is written, so nothing can be written through one. - **A kept archive stays as it was.** With `--keep-archive`, the code that shrinks, frees or deletes archive bytes refuses to run for the whole extraction, and its progress file has a format older versions refuse, so none of them can resume it in place. What it cannot protect against: if the download itself is damaged, the files before the damaged spot are extracted and the archive is partly gone. Use `--verify-first` when the archive can't be downloaded again. On btrfs or APFS, space held by a snapshot that includes the archive is not freed until the snapshot is deleted. ## Supported formats | Format | Status | Freed in steps of | |---|---|---| | ZIP, ZIP64, self-extracting `.exe` ZIPs | Supported. Tested: Stored, Deflate, Deflate64, bzip2, LZMA, PPMd, XZ and Zstandard, including archives made by 7-Zip itself, and entries past the 4 GiB mark. | One file | | 7z, solid and non-solid | Supported. Tested with archives made by 7-Zip 25.01: LZMA2 (its default), LZMA, BCJ with LZMA2, bzip2, Deflate and PPMd; Zstandard with an archive made by py7zr, since 7-Zip has no Zstandard coder for the 7z format. | One solid block | | tar (uncompressed) | Supported, including long names, symlinks and hard links | One file | | `.tar.gz`, `.tgz` | Supported, including multi-member gzip (`bgzip`, `pigz -i`) and split `.tar.gz.001` sets. Extracted from the front, freeing the compressed bytes behind the decoder where the filesystem can punch holes; every gzip CRC-32 and length is checked before anything is touched. Tested with archives from GNU tar with gzip, and pigz. Elsewhere (FAT32, exFAT) it still extracts and resumes, but needs room for the archive and every file at once, and `check` says so. | 256 MiB of output | | Split archives (`.001`, `.002`, ...) of ZIP or 7z, as 7-Zip makes them | Supported | One file or block; each volume is deleted once emptied | | Password-protected ZIP (ZipCrypto and AES) and 7z (AES, including encrypted file lists) | Supported. HatchZip asks for the password, or takes `--password` or `HATCHZIP_PASSWORD`, and proves it on one file before anything is deleted. It is never saved, so a resumed run asks again. | Same as unencrypted | | `.tar.zst`, `.tar.xz` | Refused before extraction, planned; see [the format notes](docs/formats.md#tarzst-and-tarxz). | | | One huge solid 7z block | Works, but needs free space for the whole block, as the table above shows. Freeing space inside a block is the same planned technique. | | | RAR, RAR 5 and RAR 4, single files and volume sets (`.part1.rar`, `.part2.rar`, ... or `.rar`, `.r00`, ...) | Supported in the release builds, decoded by UnRAR (see [License](#license)); builds without the `rar` feature, such as `cargo install hatchzip`, refuse RAR before anything is touched. Password-protected files work as for ZIP: a RAR 5 password is proven by its check value, a RAR 4 one by decoding the smallest encrypted file, which for a large file can take a while. A large stored file is freed while it is written, as in tar. Refused before anything is touched: encrypted file names, links, dictionaries over 4 GB, and sets with a volume missing or a stray one after the last. `restore` works. Tested with archives made by RAR 6.24 (RAR 5 and RAR 4) and archives written by the test suite; sets made by WinRAR 7.23 were tested on Windows when RAR support was first written. | One file; a volume once every file that reaches into it is out | | Solid RAR | Extracted only while the archive is kept (`--keep-archive`): a solid archive decodes front to back in one pass and UnRAR can't save its state, so it can't be freed as it goes or resumed mid-way. In place, it is refused before anything is touched. | | | Native split ZIP (`.z01`) | Planned | | ## How it works ZIP, 7z and tar all store their contents as a sequence of independent pieces: files for ZIP and tar, solid blocks for 7z. ZIP and 7z keep their index at the very end. HatchZip saves that index to a side file, then extracts pieces starting from the last one in the archive. After each batch it truncates the archive to where that batch began, which every operating system and filesystem supports; for a split archive, that means deleting whole volumes and shortening one. RAR stores files one after another like tar, so it is freed file by file too, and a volume is deleted once every file reaching into it is out. A `.tar.gz` is one compressed stream that can only be decoded from the front, so HatchZip extracts it front to back and punches holes in the compressed bytes it has used, at resume points it can restart from after a crash. The full design, including the exact order of writes that makes a crash safe, is in [How it works](docs/how-it-works.md). ## How it is built HatchZip is written with the help of AI coding assistants, and [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) is the rulebook they work under. It is the strict part of the project: the tool deletes its own input, so a change only lands with proof. - **More than 130 tests run on Linux, macOS and Windows** for every change, in CI on real machines of each kind. - **Crash tests kill the process at every step** where it writes a file, saves its progress or cuts the archive, then resume and compare every extracted file byte for byte. - **Freeing space is checked, not assumed.** CI fails if ext4, APFS or NTFS do not really give the space back. - **Damaged and hostile archives are part of the suite:** paths that escape the folder, overlapping entries, bad CRCs, truncated downloads, wrong passwords. - **Every number in this README was measured** on real hardware, and the conditions are written next to it. Pull requests and bug reports from people are held to the same rules, and are very welcome. ## Star history ## License HatchZip is licensed under either of [Apache License, Version 2.0](LICENSE-APACHE) or [MIT license](LICENSE-MIT), at your option. RAR archives are decoded by the UnRAR source code, which is freeware under its own [license](LICENSE-UNRAR): free to use for extracting RAR archives, but not to build a RAR compatible archiver. It is compiled in only with the `rar` cargo feature, which is off by default, so `cargo install hatchzip`, the crates on crates.io and distribution builds are open source throughout and need no C++ compiler. The release builds on the [releases page](https://github.com/xevrion/hatchzip/releases) have it on, and every release download includes `LICENSE-UNRAR`. ## Contributing Bug reports, especially from filesystems and operating systems not covered by CI, are welcome. Read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) first. Unless you explicitly state otherwise, any contribution intentionally submitted for inclusion in HatchZip by you, as defined in the Apache-2.0 license, shall be dual licensed as above, without any additional terms or conditions.

然后在浏览器里打开一个编辑器等你。哪里不满意，在画面上点一下，写下要改什么，它就只改那一处。 ```sh npx skills add alchaincyf/huashu-motion ``` [看效果](#看效果) · [安装](#安装) · [能做什么](#能做什么) · [怎么做到的](#怎么做到的) · [背后的故事](#背后的故事)
--- ## 看效果 这篇README里的每一段动画都是huashu-motion做的。上面那段取自它给自己做的53秒发布片，👉 [下载完整发布片（MP4，带声音）](https://github.com/alchaincyf/huashu-motion/releases/latest)，下面Grok Bot、huashu-design、DeepSeek这几支的完整版也在同一个页面。 ### 指着画面改 按C，在画面上点一下，写下要改什么。评论发过去的时候带着时间点、场景、点中的元素和它在源码里的位置，agent先把那一帧和你点的那一小块截图放大看一眼，再只改那一处，改完回一句人话，预览停在原来的位置刷新。每一版都留着，⌘Z随时撤回；标题、数字、颜色、停留时长这些会变成编辑器右边的输入框，自己改，不用等agent。 （这段里的编辑器和终端是照真实界面重建的，代码细节是示意；评论是真实提过的意见。） ### 先写谱，再拍片 做发布片用的是作曲家模式：agent按节奏单先写一份谱（ABC记谱法，纯文本的乐谱），谱里的标记对齐每个场景，再由三角钢琴、弦乐和鼓组的采样演奏出来（真乐器采样要先跑一次`om samples build`，不跑就用合成音色）；画面上每个东西落地的那一帧，再配一个音效。配乐全部在本机现场生成，不调用任何收费接口。 ### 一天，二十支 16个镜头，来自同一天做的七支片子，按拍子切。 Grok Bot（粉丝自制，非官方）· 30秒：傍晚交代任务，夜里几个agent各干各的，早上7点手机上收到汇报。这段是汇报一张张送往Chief of Staff的那几拍。

huashu-design 3.0 · 一句提示词钉住不动，背后的风格按拍子换
小猫补光灯Pro · 八种补光色，一拍换一种
### 不依赖Opus：DeepSeek V4.1 Flash也能做 这支22秒的动效片，是把Claude Code背后的模型换成DeepSeek V4.1 Flash（1017版）做的。中间我给了三轮意见（比如加上DeepSeek的鲸鱼logo、删掉几个镜头），带配乐和音效，前后不到半小时，按当时的价格花了1块9毛5（缓存命中率99.4%）。统一的配色、贯穿全片的那颗圆点、卡在124BPM上的配乐，是skill带出来的，我一句都没提过。方法写进了skill，便宜的模型也能拍出像样的片子。 --- ## 安装 ### 方式一：跟你的agent说（推荐） ``` 帮我安装huashu-motion这个skill（github.com/alchaincyf/huashu-motion），装好后跑一遍demo ``` ### 方式二：一行命令 ```sh npx skills add alchaincyf/huashu-motion ``` [skills](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills)会认出你在用的agent，把skill放进对应目录；要指定的话加`-a claude-code`、`-a codex`等参数。 Claude Code、Codex、WorkBuddy、Grok Bot、Muse、Dots等产品都能跑；它遵循[Agent Skills](https://agentskills.io)协议，支持skill的agent都能装。 ### 方式三：克隆整个仓库
展开查看 ```sh git clone https://github.com/alchaincyf/huashu-motion.git ln -s "$PWD/huashu-motion/skills/huashu-motion" ~/.claude/skills/huashu-motion # Codex换成~/.codex/skills/ ``` skill里的`bin/om`会直接调用仓库里的命令行工具，改仓库就是改skill，本机只有一份。
### 需要什么 - Node 22以上。 - Chrome（或Chromium、Edge）：截帧、检查、导出都用你电脑上已经装好的浏览器，不额外下载渲染器。 - FFmpeg：导出视频、合成配乐要用。 - 真乐器音色（可选）：想要三角钢琴、弦乐、鼓组，让agent跑一次`om samples build`，下载约55MB的免费采样（CC0和CC-BY授权）；不跑就用合成音色。 - 口播（可选）：macOS的系统音色不用装；想用Kokoro念中文稿，第一次用时会给出一行安装命令（要uv和Python 3.12，模型约325MB）；逐字对齐要装whisper-cli（`brew install whisper-cpp`）。 缺什么跑`om doctor`就知道，这些都可以直接让agent帮你装。目前只在macOS上实测过。Codex的沙箱会拦本地预览和浏览器，遇到时手动批准一下。 --- ## 能做什么 装好以后，直接跟agent说： | 你说 | 它做 | |---|---| | 「用huashu-motion给我的产品做一支30秒的发布片，官网是xxx.com」 | 先读产品，出三个方向的关键帧给你挑，写节奏单，再写片、作曲配乐，打开编辑器等你 | | 「把data/funnel.csv做成30秒解说，讲清楚为什么注册率翻倍了」 | 按数据讲故事：先轴、后数据、只标一件事，数字变成可以直接改的输入框 | | 「做一支发布片，要口播，用我自己的录音：voice.m4a」 | 逐字对齐，画面落在说到的那个词上，自动出字幕，配乐在说话时让位 | | 「这条口播视频加个包装」 | 名字条、数字卡、关键词花字、章节卡，导出带透明通道的叠层，直接拖进剪映或Premiere | | 「改成竖屏」 | 复制一份1080×1920的版本，重新排版的活儿进收件箱，接着改 | | 「导出GIF」「要透明底」「做成网页分享」 | MP4、MOV（透明）、WebM、GIF；或者导出一个带播放器和源码的分享页 | 开工前，它会先读你以前的偏好和过去片子留下的经验；每支片子做完，再把你这次说过的话、在编辑器里提的评论收一遍，值得留下的记下来。你的偏好只存在你自己电脑上。 --- ## 怎么做到的 ### 一支片子就是一个`index.html` 画面用代码写，GSAP、Canvas、Three.js、SVG，浏览器能画的都能用；不调用视频生成模型，每一帧只由代码和时间决定。没有私有格式，片子就是一个网页，带走就能用。 ``` 你的agent ──写──▶ my-film/index.html ◀──盯着── om studio（浏览器里的编辑器） ▲ │ └── om inbox --wait ◀── .om/inbox.jsonl ◀── 你在画面上点一下、写一句 ``` ### 导演规则，不是模板 skill最大的一块是导演方法：先读产品、找出它的气质，再选片子的结构和运动语言。这些规则来自实测，不是拍脑袋： - 拿21支真实的发布片（Apple、Nothing、GoPro、Google、Vercel、Linear、Anthropic等），用FFmpeg逐支量切点、节拍、响度和能量曲线； - 拆了142支高互动的发布片和动效片，按产品类型整理出20种运动语言，每种写清楚它在说什么、适合什么产品； - 每支片子开工前先写一张节奏单：3秒内要有钩子，中段要有一次爆发，最响的那一下前面先停一拍。 颜色也量过：顶级发布片的颜色几乎都是找来的（品牌色、产品外壳和界面、实拍里的光），所以三个方向先从产品里找颜色，`om swatch`把色板和对比度摆出来看。 ### 声音是片子的一半 - 作曲家模式：agent写谱，程序用真乐器采样演奏，谱里的场景标记对齐画面；仓库里带了三份有注释的示范谱。 - 兜底配乐：不想作曲，内置12类产品、每类3种配乐方向，按片子的种子挑，不喜欢可以重抽。 - 23种音效：落地、甩镜、打字、盖章、故障……写在动画落地的那一行代码上，导出时自动对上。 - 口播：系统音色念稿，或者用你自己的录音；逐字对齐，画面可以落在某个词上。 ### 自己的渲染引擎 渲染、截帧、检查都直接驱动你电脑上的Chrome：按CPU核数开几个浏览器同时渲染（默认最多8个），配乐和画面并行编码，配乐没改就直接复用。一支30秒的片子，在我这台14核的Mac上大约12–15秒渲完；加运动模糊大约1到1.5分钟。 ### 交付前有人挑错 - `om check`：渲染前查脚本、缺失的文件、违反规则的动画写法，再抽帧查被裁切、被盖住、对比度不够的字； - `om qa`：查成片里一闪而过的单帧、没东西在动的空档、硬切和整片的运动曲线； - skill要求agent交付前真的看帧、按正常速度看一遍，能派独立的agent冷审就派。 ### 常用命令 平时都是agent在敲，想自己动手也可以： | 命令 | 做什么 | |---|---| | `om new` · `om templates` | 新建项目，可以从10个模板起步 | | `om studio` | 编辑器：实时预览、场景条、直接改值、在画面上留评论 | | `om inbox --wait` · `om look` · `om done` | agent那一侧：接下一条评论、看你点的位置、回报改了什么 | | `om sound` · `om voice` · `om samples` | 配乐和音效、口播、真乐器采样包 | | `om check` · `om qa` · `om still` | 渲染前检查、成片检查、任意时刻截一帧 | | `om render` · `om export html` · `om fork` | 导出、分享页、换画幅 | | `om learn` · `om undo` · `om doctor` | 经验、撤回、环境检查 | --- ## 里面有什么 | | 数量 | |---|---| | 运动语言（每种写清楚它在说什么、适合什么、怎么做） | 20种，`skills/huashu-motion/references/library/` | | 起步模板（发布会、财经图表、动态文字、白板、Vox拼贴、3Blue1Brown、Kurzgesagt、口播包装……） | 10个，`templates/` | | 音效 | 23种 | | 兜底配乐方向 | 12类产品 × 3种 | | 示范谱 | 3份，`skills/huashu-motion/references/scores/` | | 字体（中文500–900字重、衬线、展示字体） | 27款，`fonts/` | | 方法文档（导演、节奏、颜色、声音、口播、产品演示、验收……） | `skills/huashu-motion/references/` | ``` huashu-motion/ ├── skills/huashu-motion/ # skill本体：SKILL.md、方法文档、运动语言库、示范谱、经验 ├── cli/ # om命令行：新建、编辑器、收件箱、配乐、口播、检查、渲染、导出 ├── runtime/ # 片子里用的OM.*小工具，和逐帧渲染的引擎 ├── studio/ # 浏览器里的编辑器 ├── templates/ # 10个起步模板 ├── fonts/ # 随附的开源字体 ├── examples/ # 样片（om demo打开的那支） └── test/ # 测试 ``` --- ## 诚实边界 - 它听不见。agent靠谱面、能量曲线和频谱图检查配乐，最后一耳朵还得是你的。 - 它不会凭空生成真人和实拍。画面全是代码画的；要真人、实拍，用你自己的素材，它负责合成和包装。 - 效果跟模型有关。我主要在Claude Code里用Opus 5.5；DeepSeek V4.1 Flash也能做得不错，但不同模型的品味差别是真实存在的。 - 要能跑命令的环境。预览和导出在本机跑，需要Node、Chrome和FFmpeg。 --- ## 背后的故事 2026年10月8号，Anthropic发布了Claude Motion，让Claude用代码把报告、图表、产品讲解做成短动画，可以指着画面改，发布时只在Team和Enterprise上beta。 今年4月Claude Design出来的时候，我把它的核心能力逆向成了skill，就是后来的[huashu-design](https://github.com/alchaincyf/huashu-design)。Motion发布以后，我让Claude Code开工，要求就一句： > 我们的skill需要能够完整复刻claude motion的能力，并且要强很多！ 第一天做出来的东西，我看着都很无聊：编辑器、版本管理、一百多项测试都有了，一个19秒的3D城市样片，运镜很平稳，也就代表着很平庸。让Claude自己把项目审一遍，它的结论是：做出了一个很会证明自己没撒谎的工程，却还没有一个让人想转发的作品。当天推倒重来。 后来真正花时间的，是让片子好看：去量真实的发布片，给配乐提「电影级别」的要求，把每一次「不酷」「无聊」「字体难看」都变成规则写回skill。最后它给自己做了一支发布片，就是这篇README最上面那段。 --- ## 致谢 - 动画库[GSAP](https://gsap.com)（GSAP Standard License），随附字体均为SIL OFL 1.1开源字体，清单见`fonts/LICENSES.md`。 - 真乐器采样来自CC0和CC-BY授权的开源采样库，`om samples build`时从原处下载，不随仓库分发；口播用到[Kokoro](https://github.com/thewh1teagle/kokoro-onnx)和[whisper.cpp](https://github.com/ggml-org/whisper.cpp)，第一次用时下载模型。详见[THIRD_PARTY.md](THIRD_PARTY.md)。 - 导演规则里量过、拆过的发布片和动效片，仓库只记测量出来的参数，不含它们的画面。 - `om demo`打开的样片用的是[huashu-art-motion](https://github.com/alchaincyf/huashu-art-motion)的绘画引擎。 --- ## 关于作者 **花叔 Huashu** — AI Native Coder，独立开发者，代表作：小猫补光灯（AppStore 付费榜 Top1） | | | |:---|:---| | 🌐 官网 | [bookai.top](https://bookai.top) · [huasheng.ai](https://www.huasheng.ai) | | 𝕏 Twitter | [@AlchainHust](https://x.com/AlchainHust) | | 📺 B站 | [花叔v](https://space.bilibili.com/14097567) | | ▶️ YouTube | [@Alchain](https://www.youtube.com/@Alchain) | | 📕 小红书 | [花叔](https://www.xiaohongshu.com/user/profile/5abc6f17e8ac2b109179dfdf) | | 💬 公众号 | 微信搜「花叔」 | ## 许可证 代码和文档：MIT。随便用，随便改，随便造。 随附的第三方部分保留各自的许可：GSAP（GSAP Standard License）、字体（SIL OFL 1.1），见[THIRD_PARTY.md](THIRD_PARTY.md)。 例外：「豆子花叔」角色（`runtime/clip/lib/toon.js`里的角色绘制，以及它在storytime模板和示范片里的形象）是花叔的卡通形象，只用于本项目的示范，不随MIT授权用于其他用途。 ---

# 3D Model Anything

[![Watch the video: 3D Model Anything](docs/images/thumb-1.png)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JGQCcCzuS88)

Capture a room on an iPhone, then use its geometry and photographs to build an editable Three.js scene with an AI coding agent.

[Open the office viewer](https://wesbos.github.io/3d-model-anything/) · [App support](https://wesbos.github.io/3d-model-anything/support.html)

This repository includes the **3D Model Anything iPhone app**, a **Three.js viewer**, the **scan-to-threejs agent skill**, and **Wes’s detailed office demo**.

The app records the evidence. The skill guides an agent through measurement, modeling and matched-camera visual comparisons. This is an iterative reconstruction workflow, not a one-click scan-to-perfect-model converter. The current workflow focuses on rooms and interiors.

## Run the viewer

Use Node.js 22.12+ (or a newer supported release).

```sh
npm ci
npm run dev
```

Open http://localhost:5188. Explore the office in dollhouse, walking, overhead, wireframe and knolling views. The playground is at `/play.html?room=office-v4&mode=fpv`.

```sh
npm run build
npm run preview
```

The demo includes the reconstructed office and selected textures. Original scans and photo collections are not distributed; Scan and Overlay are disabled for this example. Those modes remain available for your own rooms with reference assets.

## Capture your own space

See [the iPhone app](apps/house-capture/README.md) for building with Xcode, device requirements, scanning and sharing. Scanning needs a LiDAR-equipped iPhone or iPad. Non-LiDAR devices can import and review scans.

The app is source-available here; an App Store release is a separate distribution step. Do not assume an App Store download is available yet.

Export a room or session through the system share sheet and extract it into an ignored `data/captures-in/<room>/` directory. Exports keep the existing `house-capture/5` contract; changing the app name does not change the files.

## Use the skill

The skill lives at `.agents/skills/scan-to-threejs/SKILL.md`. Open this repository in an agent that supports local skills and ask it to use **scan-to-threejs** with your extracted export. You can also copy that skill directory into your agent's skill directory; the companion viewer/runtime in this repo is still needed for its capture workflow.

Example request:

> Use scan-to-threejs to rebuild the room in data/captures-in/my-room. Inspect the measurements and photos, create an editable scene, and compare rendered views with the original photographs.

Start with [the format guide](.agents/skills/scan-to-threejs/references/house-capture.md) and [project layout](.agents/skills/scan-to-threejs/references/project-layout.md). Helpers need Python 3; photo comparisons need Pillow, and optional depth reconstruction needs NumPy, Open3D and Pillow. Capture scripts use the `agent-browser` CLI.

A new room goes in `demos/<id>/` and is registered in `demos/index.ts`. The office example retains its earlier reconstruction layers (`office-v2`, `office-latest`, `office-v4`) to preserve the final geometry.

## Privacy and licensing

Only the office example is distributed. No other rooms, connected-house layout, original scan bundles, or development Git history are included. Keep your captures private; inspect assets before publishing your own demo.

Reusable source code and the skill are MIT licensed. The supplied office images/textures have separate [asset terms](ASSETS-LICENSE.md). Third-party marks, artwork and depicted products are not licensed by the code license.

See [release status](docs/release-status.md) for validation and iPhone distribution steps.

🧹 Removes the junk
Bloatware, ads and sponsored rows, gone.		 📺 A calm home screen
Your apps, your HDMI inputs and a clock. Nothing else.		 ↩️ Undo anytime
Apps are turned off, never deleted.
## Watch it work **[▶ Claude Made My Old Android TV Feel Brand New](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fP2SGGVsaB0)** · the full setup on a real TV, in 4 minutes. ## Get started **1. Turn on developer mode on the TV.** Settings → Device Preferences → About → press **Build** 7 times. Then turn on **USB debugging** in **Developer options**. [Stuck?](#help) Read the [notes and warnings](#notes-and-warnings) first. **2. Open [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) or [Codex](https://openai.com/codex) on your laptop.** The laptop and TV must be on the same Wi-Fi. **3. Paste this in.** ```text Help me clean up my Android TV and make it faster. My TV is a . 1. Before you change anything, tell me in plain words: this turns off system apps, and that has some risk. A few TVs got stuck at the logo or kept restarting, and you're an AI, so you can make mistakes. undo.sh and your undo list turn everything back on. Ask me to confirm I want to go ahead. 2. Connect to my TV over Wi-Fi. Walk me through anything I need to tap on the TV. 3. Before changing anything, list every app in plain English: safe to turn off, needed by the TV, and apps I use. Check free memory. 4. Ask me before every change. Turn apps off instead of deleting them. Keep a list of what you changed and how to undo it. 5. Never turn off: Google Play services (com.google.android.gms), Google Play, Settings, System UI, setup apps, the keyboard, Bluetooth, my HDMI inputs, the TV's input and tuner framework, or anything else the TV needs to start. On Google TV or Chromecast, also never turn off Google TV's home screen (com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx). If you're not sure, leave it on. 6. Install the home screen: download https://github.com/Ansub/tv-detox and run its install.sh with my TV and these apps: . 7. Turn off animations and make the TV sleep after 5 minutes. Then check the model name and ask me if the TV is OLED. Keep the screensaver on unless I say it's not OLED. 8. Wait 30 seconds after the last change, then restart the TV once and check it starts up normally before you say you're done. Show me free memory before and after. 9. Once everything is checked, remind me to turn off USB, Network and Wireless debugging (or Developer options) on the TV. Left on, other devices on my network can ask to control it. I only turn it back on for undo.sh or updates. ``` That's it. It asks you before every change. **4. Turn debugging off when it's done.** In **Developer options**, turn off **USB debugging**, plus **Network debugging** or **Wireless debugging** if you turned them on. Or turn off **Developer options** completely. ### Notes and warnings > [!WARNING] > **Do it at your own risk.** This turns off system apps. A few TVs got stuck at the logo or kept restarting, and the AI can make mistakes. It asks you before every change, and [`undo.sh`](#undo) plus its undo list turn everything back on. This is what worked for us, not professional advice. You're responsible for your own TV, and I'm not liable if something goes wrong. > [!WARNING] > **Google TV and Chromecast with Google TV:** don't turn off the TV's own home screen. On some of these devices that left them stuck restarting, and the only fix was a factory reset. Since v1.4.1, `install.sh` leaves it on for Google TV unless you opt in with `GOOGLE_TV=1`. The cleanup still works and makes the TV faster. You just keep Google TV's own home screen. > [!WARNING] > **OLED TVs:** keep the screensaver on. It stops a still picture from burning into the screen. Don't leave any home screen, this one included, on for hours. > [!NOTE] > **Turn debugging off afterwards.** While USB, Network or Wireless debugging is on, other devices on your network can ask to control the TV. Turn it off once setup is done, and back on only to run `undo.sh` or update. ## Help
How do I turn on developer mode?
1. On the TV, open **Settings**, then **Device Preferences** (or **System**), then **About**. 2. Press OK on **Build** 7 times until you see "You are now a developer." 3. Go back, open **Developer options** and turn on **USB debugging**. If you see **Network debugging** or **Wireless debugging**, turn that on too. 4. The first time your laptop connects, the TV asks "Allow debugging?" Tick "Always allow" and press **Allow**. 5. When setup is done, turn **USB debugging**, **Network debugging** and **Wireless debugging** off again (or turn off **Developer options**). Turn them back on only to run `undo.sh` or update. **Chromecast with Google TV and other newer Google TVs** usually only have **Wireless debugging**, which needs a pairing code. `install.sh ` alone won't connect. Instead: 1. In **Developer options**, open **Wireless debugging** and choose **Pair device with pairing code**. Leave that screen open. 2. On your laptop, run `adb pair :` with the IP and port shown under the code, and type the code. 3. Back on the **Wireless debugging** screen, note the IP and port shown there (it's a different port), and run `adb connect :`. 4. Use that same address for every script: `sh install.sh :`, `sh undo.sh :`. The port changes every time the TV restarts, and the connection can drop. If a script says it can't reach the TV, pair and connect again. Don't restart the TV halfway through a cleanup. Menus differ a bit by brand. If you're stuck, ask Claude or Codex: *"I have a \ TV. How can you connect to it from my laptop and take control of it?"*
Which TVs does it work on?
Android TV 9 (a real TV), 11 and 12, and Google TV 14 (also a real TCL TV, see [TCL notes](#tcl-notes)). Every change is tested automatically on emulators.
Can I do this on a Fire TV, Roku, Samsung or LG?
- **Amazon Fire TV:** partly. Fire TV is Android underneath, so the cleanup works. Amazon blocks changing the home screen on current Fire TVs, so you keep Amazon's. Tell Claude what you want to keep, like Alexa voice search on the remote. - **Roku:** no. Roku runs its own system, not Android, so nothing can connect to it to turn things off. - **Samsung (Tizen):** no, for the same reason. - **LG (webOS):** no. You can still cut down the ads by turning off **Home Promotion** and **Content Recommendation** in the TV's home settings. If your TV or streaming box runs Android TV or Google TV, it should work. That includes many Sony, TCL, Hisense, Philips and Xiaomi TVs, Chromecast with Google TV and Nvidia Shield. Some of those brands also sell Roku or other non-Android models, so check **Settings > About** if you're not sure.
What about projectors or Android phones?
- **Android projectors:** probably. If it has **Developer options** and **USB debugging**, the cleanup should work. Cheap projectors often run a custom Android, so the home screen may act a bit differently. - **Android phones:** only the cleanup. The home screen is made for a TV remote, not touch.
Anything to watch out for on Chromecast with Google TV?
The cleanup works, but **leave Google TV's own home screen on**, which means you keep Google TV's home screen. At least one Chromecast got stuck restarting after it was turned off, and it needed a factory reset. `install.sh` leaves it on by default since v1.4.1. - Connect with Wireless debugging (see "How do I turn on developer mode?" above). The plain `install.sh ` won't reach a Chromecast. - The YouTube button on the remote can stop working, and some lose casting. Tell Claude to keep casting on if you use it.
Home opens Google TV's setup screen instead (Sony BRAVIA and others)
On some Google TVs, once Google TV's home screen (`com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx`) is off, Android picks the setup app (`com.google.android.tungsten.setupwraith`) for Home instead. `install.sh` spots this and asks before turning the setup app off too. It only asks if Home opens exactly that app, Google TV's home screen is already off and the TV has finished its first setup. Since v1.4.1 this only happens if you also opt in with `GOOGLE_TV=1`. `YES=1` doesn't turn it off; use `YES_SETUP=1` for that. This worked on a Sony BRAVIA and a TCL Smart TV Pro (Google TV 14), but it hasn't been tested on every TV. `undo.sh` turns it back on. To undo it by hand: ```sh adb shell pm enable com.google.android.tungsten.setupwraith adb shell pm enable com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx ``` If the TV ever asks to be set up again, or a setup screen won't finish, turn the setup app back on first.
TCL TVs: what worked, and what to keep
Tested on a TCL Smart TV Pro (Google TV, Android 14, 2.3 GB of RAM). Every step below was followed by a restart, and the TV started normally each time. Free memory went from about 660 MB to about 1 GB, though part of that is just from restarting: the first number was taken after the TV had been on for 15 days. **Home screen.** With Google TV's home screen off, Home opened the setup app's recovery screen, as in [#16](https://github.com/Ansub/tv-detox/issues/16). Turning the setup app off too (`YES_SETUP=1`) made this home screen stick, through several restarts. **Connect on port 5555.** If you connected with **Wireless debugging** (pairing code), turning the setup app off ends that connection halfway through `install.sh`. The script then says it couldn't turn the setup app off, even though it did. On this TV, the classic port also worked, so you can reconnect with `adb connect :5555`, check with `adb shell pm list packages -d`, and run `install.sh` again with that address. **Safe to turn off**, if you don't use them: | App | Package | |---|---| | TCL account | `com.tcl.usercenter` | | Built-in manual | `com.tcl.ocean.instructions` | | TCL Channel (free channels with ads) | `com.tcl.channelplus` | | TCL recommendations | `com.tcl.waterfall.overseas` | | TCL notifications and promos | `com.tcl.messagebox` | | Store demo | `com.tcl.esticker`, `com.tcl.exhibit` | | Alexa built-in | `com.tcl.smartalexa` | | Phone link | `com.tcl.magiconnectfree` | | Repair guide, logs | `com.tcl.repairguide`, `com.tcl.logkit` | | Screen mirroring | `com.tcl.miracast` | | TCL analytics and Alexa hooks | `com.tcl.ttvs` | | TCL interactive and ads service | `com.tcl.interactive` | | Game bar for consoles | `com.tcl.gamebar` | | Photo viewer, USB media player | `com.tcl.gallery`, `com.tcl.ui_mediaCenter` | | App manager | `com.tcl.guard` | | Bluetooth "listen alone" | `com.tcl.t_solo` | | Google TV's screensaver (about 200 MB, keep it on an OLED TV) | `com.google.android.apps.tv.dreamx` | **Tiles that stay after the cleanup.** Two TCL tiles can still show up on this home screen. **TCL Channel** is `com.tcl.partnercustomizer`, which also handles the TCL button on the remote. **TCL Home** is `com.tcl.dashboard`, TCL's quick settings panel. Both turned off without trouble. **Keep these on:** - `com.tcl.tvinput`: the HDMI inputs and the tuner. - `com.tcl.suspension`: the input picker. - `com.tcl.inputmethod.international`: the TCL keyboard. - `com.tcl.providers.config`: other TCL apps read their settings from it. - `com.tcl.useragreement`: TCL's privacy switches. `com.tcl.tv` is Live TV, the channel guide and channel scanning. Turn it off only if you never watch antenna or cable TV. **Optional: the phone keyboard keeps popping up.** On this TV, Google TV's phone-remote service made its phone keyboard the TV's keyboard again after every restart. If that happens to you, first note which keyboard you have now: ```sh adb shell settings get secure default_input_method ``` Then switch to the TCL keyboard and turn the phone-remote service off: ```sh adb shell ime set com.tcl.inputmethod.international/.T_IME adb shell pm disable-user --user 0 com.google.android.tv.remote.service ``` This also stops your phone from working as a remote: no typing, voice search or control from the Google TV or Google Home app. `undo.sh` doesn't undo it. To undo it by hand, turn the service back on and switch back to the keyboard you noted: ```sh adb shell pm enable com.google.android.tv.remote.service adb shell ime set ``` **The TCL logo at startup** is part of the TV's firmware, so it can't be turned off. On this TV, turning it off with the remote (not at the wall) let TCL's quick start wake it straight to the home screen, with no logo.
OnePlus TVs: what worked, and what to keep
Tested on a OnePlus TV E00 (QLED, Android TV 11 with Google TV's home screen, 2.9 GB of RAM). The cleanup was followed by a restart, and the TV started normally and opened this home screen by itself. Free memory went from about 1.34 GB to about 1.67 GB, though part of that is just from restarting. **Home screen.** OnePlus ships two home screens: OxygenPlay (`com.oneplus.tv.launcher`) and Google TV's (`com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx`). Turning off Google TV's is up to you and at your own risk: it worked on this TV, but it has left some Google TVs (like Chromecast) stuck restarting. Only try it if you can reconnect over USB or port 5555. If you leave it on, the cleanup still works and Home keeps opening Google TV's home screen. If you do turn it off and Home opens Google TV's setup app, run `install.sh` again with `GOOGLE_TV=1 YES_SETUP=1`, the same fix as on the TCL above. **Safe to turn off**, if you don't use them: | App | Package | |---|---| | OxygenPlay home screen | `com.oneplus.tv.launcher` | | OnePlus message board and promos | `com.heytap.tv.msgboard` | | Store demo | `fusion.android.tv.demo` | | User guide | `com.oneplus.tv.userguide` | | Weather | `net.oneplus.weather` | | ColorOS Relax | `com.coloros.relax.tv` | | Screen mirroring (Miracast) | `com.heytap.optvmiracastservice` | | OnePlus phone link | `com.heytap.olink`, `com.heytap.ars.sink` | | Bluetooth speaker mode | `com.heytap.tv.btspeaker` | | Camera | `com.heytap.tv.camera` | | AirScreen | `com.ionitech.airscreen` | **Keep these on:** - `com.heytap.tv.livetv`: Live TV, which also opens the HDMI input list. Turning it off can stop you switching inputs. - `com.mediatek.*`, `com.oneplus.tv.factory`, `com.oneplus.tv.remote`: the remote's buttons, the input key, the tuner and HDMI. **Remote buttons.** If you turned Google TV's home screen off, the **Guide** and **All apps** keys do nothing, because they open it. That's expected.
The Claude app says it can't reach my TV
The chat in the Claude app (and claude.ai) runs on Anthropic's servers, not on your laptop, so it can't see your TV. You need something that runs on your own laptop: [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) or [Codex](https://openai.com/codex). Don't want to pay for either? Skip the AI and use `install.sh` instead (see "Can I install the home screen without AI?" below).
Can I do it from my phone, without a laptop?
Not yet. Claude has to run on a computer on the same network as your TV. A phone hotspot is fine as that network, as long as the laptop and TV both join it.
My TV is on Ethernet, not Wi-Fi
That works the same. Your laptop talks to the TV over its IP address on your home network, so cable or Wi-Fi doesn't matter. The laptop just has to be on the same network. You'll find the TV's IP in its network settings, or ask Claude to find it.
Can I just do the cleanup and keep my TV's home screen?
Yes. Leave out step 5 of the prompt ("Install the home screen"). Your TV looks the same, just with the junk turned off.
How do I know which apps are safe to turn off?
Run the planner. It reads the TV and prints every app with a verdict, changing nothing: ```sh sh candidates.sh ``` `never` the TV needs it, `keep` it carries a feature you may use, `safe` common junk, `review` unknown. [docs/debloat.md](docs/debloat.md) explains the rules behind the verdicts, the traps — apps Android restarts whatever you do, the app that carries casting, and package names that hide what the app really is — and the never-touch and commonly-safe lists.
Why not just use Projectivy Launcher?
You can. The cleanup is the part that makes the TV faster, and it works with any home screen. This one is here if you want something tiny and open source: one screen, no ads, no account, about 30 MB of RAM.
The TV still opens Live TV or HDMI when it turns on
That's a TV setting, not this home screen. Ask it: *"My TV opens Live TV at startup instead of the home screen. Find that setting and turn it off."*
A button on the remote stopped working
Some remote buttons are handled by the TV's own home screen or by apps the cleanup turned off. To see which app handles which button, ask Claude: *"Run `adb shell dumpsys window policy` and tell me which apps my remote's global keys go to."* If it's an app other than your TV's home screen, turn that app back on. **The YouTube button on some Google TVs** (seen on Xiaomi and Vu): it goes to Google TV's own home screen, which `install.sh` turns off, so the button does nothing. Turning that home screen back on brings the button back, but your TV may then open Google TV's home screen again instead of this one. Until there's a safe fix, open YouTube from its tile on the home screen.
An update turned something back on
```sh sh check.sh # check the home screen is still in charge sh check.sh --fix # and fix it sh check.sh --fix my-tv.txt # also check your own list of changes ``` Your list has one change per line, like `off com.example.app`, `global window_animation_scale 0` or `device_config activity_manager max_cached_processes 4`. Ask Claude to write it from the changes it made.
Can I install the home screen without AI?
Yes. You only need `adb`. On a Mac, run `brew install android-platform-tools`. On Windows, download Google's [SDK Platform Tools](https://developer.android.com/tools/releases/platform-tools), unzip it, and run the commands below from Git Bash. Download this repo, then: ```sh sh install.sh # picks your TV apps for you sh install.sh "com.netflix.ninja,com.hulu.livingroomplus" # or choose them sh install.sh "" "bluetooth,sound,picture" # add settings shortcuts ``` Most TVs keep opening their own home screen, so the script offers to turn that off. Nothing is uninstalled. The cleanup half is a judgement call per app, so it's not automated. `sh candidates.sh ` lists every app with a verdict and [docs/debloat.md](docs/debloat.md) gives the rules, if you'd rather decide yourself than have the AI do it.
How do I change the apps on the home screen?
Use the remote. Hold **OK** on an app (or press **Menu**) to: - **Move** it: use the arrows to slide it to a new spot, then press **OK** to finish. - **Replace** it: pick another app to take its place. - **Remove** it from the home screen. The app stays installed, and you can add it back any time. - **Uninstall** it, for apps you installed yourself. The TV asks you to confirm first. - **App info**, for apps that came with the TV. They can't be uninstalled, but from there you can turn them off. To add an app, pick the **Add app** tile in the bottom row. Add as many apps as you like: they wrap into rows of six, and the page scrolls once there are more than twelve. Your changes are kept until you run `install.sh` with a new app list.
Can I change the background?
Yes. Pick the **Settings** tile, then **Wallpaper**. (**TV settings**, right under it, opens the TV's own settings.) There are fourteen gradients. Dark: Dusk (the default), Midnight, Plum, Forest, Graphite, Ocean and Ember. Bright: Sunset, Lagoon, Aurora, Coral, Iris, Meadow and Gold. The background changes as you move through the list; press **OK** to keep one, or **Back** to leave it as it was. They're colours only, no pictures, so every one is just as fast and uses the same memory.
Can I get Wi-Fi and Bluetooth one press away?
Yes. A small network icon always sits next to the clock. It shows **Wi-Fi** (with signal bars), **Ethernet** or a crossed-out Wi-Fi when you're offline, and opens your network settings. **Bluetooth**, **Sound** and **Picture** shortcuts can join it. They're off unless you ask for them: ```sh sh install.sh "" "bluetooth,sound,picture" # pick any of them, in any order sh install.sh "" "none" # take them away ``` Press **Up** from your apps to reach them. A shortcut your TV has no screen for is left out. On TCL TVs, Sound and Picture open TCL's own panels.
How do I undo it?
```sh sh undo.sh ``` This turns your TV's own home screen back on and removes this one. To undo the cleanup too, ask Claude or Codex to reverse everything on its list. If you turned debugging off after setup, turn it back on first, then off again when you're done.
My TV is stuck restarting
Your laptop can often still connect for a few seconds each time the TV starts. Use that to turn everything back on: ```sh adb connect adb wait-for-device adb shell pm list packages -d ``` That lists everything that's turned off. Turn each one back on with `adb shell pm enable `, or all of them at once: ```sh for p in $(adb shell pm list packages -d | tr -d '\r' | sed 's/package://'); do adb shell pm enable "$p"; done ``` To undo just the home screen, run `sh undo.sh `. Then restart the TV. You can redo the cleanup later, one app at a time. If the laptop never connects, use the TV's recovery mode or a factory reset. How you get there depends on the brand and model, so check your TV maker's support page.
For developers: build it yourself
1. Put your default apps in `apps.txt` (package names, one per line). You can also pass them to `install.sh` instead. 2. Install Java 17 and the Android SDK. On a Mac: ```sh brew install openjdk@17 brew install --cask android-commandlinetools sdkmanager "platforms;android-34" "build-tools;34.0.0" ``` 3. `sh build.sh`, then `sh install.sh ` installs your build instead of the release. 4. `sh ci/smoke-test.sh ` checks it all works. HDMI inputs are found on their own. The labels follow the TV's language, with 16 languages built in. To add yours or fix a translation, edit `src/com/ansub/tvhome/Strings.java`. Keep `key.jks`, which is made on your first build: updates must be signed with the same key. It's one screen of plain Java, no libraries, no Gradle. The background is drawn once, the only animation is the focus lift, and it uses about 30 MB of RAM.
## Contributing Pull requests are welcome for fixes that keep working on every TV. This project sticks to official apps and Android's own settings, so changes that add ad blockers or unofficial apps won't be merged. If you want those, fork it and make it yours. ---
Made by **Ansub Khan**. I build things like this with AI every week. [**Watch on YouTube →**](https://www.youtube.com/@ansubkhan) MIT License

items.description: Take the ads, tracking and clutter out of your Fire TV over ADB, no root. Every step can be undone. Comes with its own open-source home screen.
items.readme:
Your TV should do what you paid for.
Ads, tracking and clutter out of your Fire TV. Your apps and HDMI inputs stay.

dumbtv.org · Get started · What it blocks · Devices · Get help

As seen in TechCrunch · TechRadar · Tom's Guide · Gizmodo · XDA · It's FOSS · and more than 100 others

--- ## The story I had a Fire TV Edition television that had become painful to use. Menus lagged, apps took ages to open, and the home screen was mostly ads. When I looked, it had 129 MB of free memory, and much of the rest went to apps that started on their own and to Amazon services that report what you watch. So I asked a coding agent to clean it up over ADB, and [posted what happened](https://x.com/DevMuzzammil/status/2111595814099591535). People asked for the scripts, so I put them here and [shared them](https://x.com/DevMuzzammil/status/2111912547318395338). Since then, owners of about twenty other TVs and sticks have run it and sent back what they found. dumbtv is that cleanup, made safe to run on someone else's TV. ## What it does On a Fire TV stick, Cube or Fire TV Edition television, from your computer, with no root: - **Removes the ads and tracking.** Disables Amazon's sponsored rows, ad services, screen fingerprinting (ACR), telemetry and experiments, and turns off ad tracking and usage reporting. - **Blocks what cannot be disabled.** A small open-source DNS filter on the TV stops Amazon's telemetry and automatic updates from reaching their servers. Everything else, including your streaming apps, works as before. - **Replaces the home screen** with [dumbtv home](launcher/README.md): your apps, your inputs and a clock. 54 KB, open source, no internet access, no permissions. - **Leaves your apps alone.** Nothing you watch is removed unless you name it. - **Can all be undone** with one command. ## Quick start You need a computer with [`adb`](https://developer.android.com/tools/releases/platform-tools) and about ten minutes. On the TV, turn on ADB: **Settings → My Fire TV → About**, press OK on the device name 7 times, then **Developer Options → ADB debugging**. The TV's IP address is under **Settings → My Fire TV → About → Network** (on a Fire TV Edition television: **Settings → Network**, then the connected network). **With a coding agent** (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini and others): clone this repository, open the agent in it, and say: > Clean up my Fire TV. Its IP address is _(the address from the Network screen)_. It reads [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md), asks you a few questions, and runs the steps below. **By hand:** ```sh git clone https://github.com/humblemuzzu/dumbtv && cd dumbtv adb connect :5555 # press Allow on the TV ./scripts/preflight.sh # what the TV is and what would change; changes nothing ./scripts/configure.sh # a few questions ./scripts/all.sh # asks before each step, reboots the TV twice ./scripts/verify.sh # checks the result ``` Works from macOS, Linux and Windows (WSL or Git Bash). The same steps, one at a time, are at [dumbtv.org/start](https://dumbtv.org/start). **Rather not do it yourself?** [Tell us about your TV](https://dumbtv.org/help) and we will help. ## What you choose `configure.sh` asks, and nothing is decided for you: | Question | Default | |---|---| | Do you watch Prime Video? | yes: its servers stay reachable | | Keep Alexa and the voice button? | yes | | Replace Amazon's home screen with dumbtv home? | yes | | Run the DNS filter on the TV? | yes | | Any apps you want removed? | none | | Replace the YouTube app with SmartTube (no ads, no Shorts)? | no | Your answers are saved in `dumbtv.conf`; run `configure.sh` again to change them. ## What changes | | | |---|---| | **Amazon packages** | About 50 disabled: ads, sponsored content, ACR, telemetry, crash and usage uploads, experiments, update nags. Disabled, never deleted. | | **Protected packages** | The few Amazon will not let anyone disable lose background running and background data. | | **Settings** | Ad tracking limited, interest-based ads off, usage reporting off, home-screen autoplay off. | | **DNS** | [personalDNSfilter](https://github.com/IngoZenz/personaldnsfilter) runs on the TV and blocks about 400 Amazon telemetry, ad and update hosts. YouTube, the Appstore and your other apps are not blocked. | | **Home screen** | dumbtv home instead of Amazon's: no promo tiles, no sponsored rows. | | **Your apps** | Untouched. | [How it works](docs/HOW-IT-WORKS.md) explains each part and why it is needed. An app you asked to have uninstalled comes back from the Appstore. ## Good to know - **Nothing is written to `/system`**, the part of the TV whose modification bricks it. A factory reset removes everything dumbtv did. - **Fire OS updates are blocked** while the DNS filter runs, since an update would switch a lot of this back on. [The FAQ](docs/FAQ.md) explains how to update anyway. - **It cannot replace Fire OS.** The boot chain is locked by Amazon. [Here is why](docs/WHY-NOT-REPLACE-OS.md). - **YouTube ads can't be blocked by DNS.** They come from the same servers as the videos.
